title: [Feature] Run cross-product, security, and config-hygiene suites against containerized products in CI
description:
Child of #409 (robust CI/CD epic). Split out of #421, which now covers gating only.

The per-product smoke workflows cover `connect/`, `workbench/`, `package_manager/` and `prerequisites/`. Several suites ship in `src/vip_tests/` but never execute against a real product in CI — they are only ever collected by the `--collect-only` guard in `ci.yml`, so a regression in them is invisible until a customer engagement.

## Not yet covered in CI

- `cross_product/test_integration.py`, `test_monitoring.py`, `test_resources.py`, `test_ssl.py` — need Connect + Workbench (+ PM) in the same job, which no workflow does today.
- `security/test_auth_policy.py`, `security/test_https.py` — only `security/test_error_handling.py` runs today, inside `connect-smoke.yml`.
- `config_hygiene/test_secrets.py`.

## Deliberately excluded

`performance/` (`test_load.py`, `test_concurrency.py`, `test_resource_usage.py`, `test_user_simulation.py`, `test_login_load_times.py`, `test_package_install_speed.py`) stays out: GitHub-hosted runners are too noisy for timing assertions to mean anything, and a flaky perf gate is worse than no gate. Revisit only with a dedicated runner and thresholds calibrated on it.

## Open questions

- Does the multi-product job belong in a new `cross-product-smoke.yml`, or as an extra job inside `connect-integration.yml`?
- `security/test_https.py` needs TLS terminating in front of the container — decide between a reverse-proxy sidecar and self-signed certs on the product itself.

## Acceptance

- `cross_product/`, `security/` and `config_hygiene/` run against containerized products in CI.
- Whatever gates PRs reports through an always-run Status job, consistent with the existing smoke workflows.
- `performance/` exclusion is documented in the workflow or the test package, not just in this issue.

title: [Feature] Expand Workbench smoke coverage to the full Workbench suite
description:
Child of #409 (robust CI/CD epic). Split out of #421, which now covers gating only.

`workbench-smoke.yml` runs a real Workbench container and a real `pytest` suite, but only a subset of it: `prerequisites/test_components.py`, `workbench/test_auth.py`, `workbench/test_ide_launch.py`, `workbench/test_packages.py`, `workbench/test_data_sources.py`. Connect and Package Manager smoke already run their full product suites; Workbench is the outlier.

## Not yet covered in CI

- `workbench/test_sessions.py`
- `workbench/test_session_idle.py`
- `workbench/test_session_capacity.py` (and `test_session_capacity_k8s.py`, which is likely dead after #411 removed K8s mode — confirm and delete if so)
- `workbench/test_jobs.py`
- `workbench/test_git_ops.py`
- `workbench/test_ide_extensions.py`
- `workbench/test_runtime_versions.py`
- `workbench/test_chronicle.py`
- `workbench/test_publish_to_connect.py` (needs a Connect container alongside Workbench)

## Known constraints

The smoke job runs with `-n 0` because the Docker Workbench returns "Temporary server error" on concurrent logins. Adding suites therefore adds wall-clock time serially — expect to need either the login lock from #507 or a scheduled-only tier for the slower suites.

`test_publish_to_connect.py` is the only one that needs two products in the same job.

## Acceptance

- Every Workbench test file either runs in CI against a containerized Workbench, or has a comment in the workflow saying why it cannot.
- PR-gated runtime stays acceptable; slower suites may move to the scheduled/dispatch tier rather than the PR gate.

title: fix(auth): scheme-less --connect-url defaults to http://, breaking API-key minting behind an https redirect
description:
## Summary

`vip verify --connect-url <host>` (scheme omitted) fails to mint a Connect API key against deployments that redirect HTTP→HTTPS, e.g. `connect.posit.it`. The mint step reports an HTTP error and no key is created, so all Connect API tests are then unauthenticated.

## Reproduction

```
vip verify --connect-url connect.posit.it --interactive-auth --filter via_terminal --verbose -- -n 0
```

Verbose output shows the browser opening at **`http://connect.posit.it`** (note the scheme), and the mint step then fails on a redirect.

## Root cause (two independent defects)

**1. `_normalize_url` defaults a scheme-less URL to `http://`, not `https://`** — `src/vip/config.py:35`

```python
if not url.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
    url = f"http://{url}"
```

So `connect.posit.it` becomes `http://connect.posit.it`. Defaulting bare hostnames to plaintext HTTP is wrong for essentially every modern Posit deployment and is the direct trigger here.

**2. The API-key mint client does not follow redirects** — `src/vip/auth.py:1447`

```python
with httpx.Client(
    base_url=base,
    headers=headers,
    cookies=cookies,
    timeout=scaled(10.0),
    verify=verify,
) as client:
    me_resp = client.get("/v1/user")
```

`httpx.Client` defaults to `follow_redirects=False`, so `GET http://connect.posit.it/__api__/v1/user` returns **HTTP 301 → https** and is treated as a mint failure. (`_resolve_connect_api_base` already passes `follow_redirects=True` on its probes at `auth.py:1337`/`1348`; the mint client should match.)

## Evidence

Reproduced end-to-end (`vip` 0.58.7):

- `_normalize_url("connect.posit.it")` → `'http://connect.posit.it'`
- `http://connect.posit.it/__api__/v1/user` → **HTTP 301**, `Location: https://connect.posit.it:443/__api__/v1/user`, `is_success == False`
- Against **`https://connect.posit.it`**, VIP's exact httpx mint path (session cookies + `X-Rsc-Xsrf` legacy token) returns **200** and lists/creates keys fine — so the server and mint logic are healthy; only the scheme is wrong.

## Workaround

Pass the scheme explicitly: `--connect-url https://connect.posit.it`.

## Suggested fix

1. In `_normalize_url` (`config.py`), default scheme-less URLs to `https://` instead of `http://`.
2. In the mint client (`auth.py`), add `follow_redirects=True` so minting is robust to http→https and path redirects (matching `_resolve_connect_api_base`).

Both are small and independent; doing both is recommended. Add selftests: `_normalize_url` scheme default, and a mint-client redirect-following test.

title: test_jobs.py: embedded raw newline in _JOB_SCRIPT_CONTENT breaks writeLines() console write
description:
## Summary

`test_background_job[chromium]` and `test_workbench_job[chromium]` fail at the `write_test_script` step: the `writeLines()` call typed into the RStudio console never creates `~/test_job_vip.R`, caught by the `file.exists()` check added in #528 (`VIP_JOB_SCRIPT_CHECK: FALSE`). Observed in `posit-dev/marketplaces` CI: https://github.com/posit-dev/marketplaces/actions/runs/30112200611/job/89557987527

## Root cause

```python
_JOB_SCRIPT_CONTENT = 'Sys.sleep(2)\ncat("hello from job\\n")'
...
escaped = _JOB_SCRIPT_CONTENT.replace('"', '\\"')
_run_console_command(page, f'writeLines("{escaped}", "{_JOB_SCRIPT_PATH}")')
```

`_JOB_SCRIPT_CONTENT` embeds a **real** newline character between its two R statements. The escaping only handles quotes, so that raw newline survives into the R command string passed to `_run_console_command`, which types it via Playwright's `Locator.type()`.

Playwright's keyboard layer aliases embedded `\n`/`\r` characters to the **Enter** key (`playwright-core/lib/server/input.js`: `aliases = Map([["Enter", ["\n", "\r"]]])`), so `.type()` submits the console input early, mid-statement, splitting the `writeLines(...)` call into two invalid R statements. R throws `Error: unexpected string in "cat(...)"` and the file is never written.

This has likely been broken since the tests were added in #336 — `_JOB_SCRIPT_CONTENT` and the quote-only escaping are unchanged since that commit. #528's new `file.exists()` check (v0.58.4) is what surfaced it as a clear, immediate failure instead of a downstream "script field stayed empty" symptom.

## Repro

```python
content = 'Sys.sleep(2)\ncat("hello from job\\n")'
escaped = content.replace('"', '\\"')
r_cmd = f'writeLines("{escaped}", "~/test_job_vip.R")'
assert '\n' in r_cmd  # raw newline reaches the typed command
```

Or against a live Workbench deployment:
```
uv run vip verify --workbench-url <url> --username <user> --password <pass> -f "test_background_job or test_workbench_job"
```

## Fix

Escape the embedded newline into the R string literal (`\n`, like the quotes already are) before typing, so the console receives a single line. A fix is up on `fix/job-write-script-truncation`.

title: feat(auth): add Entra ID headless-auth strategy for parity with Keycloak and Okta
description:
## Summary

Add a Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) login-form strategy to `src/vip/idp.py` so that `--headless-auth` supports Entra with the same first-class parity we already give **Keycloak** and **Okta**.

## Why this matters

**Customer prevalence.** A large share of Posit Team customers standardize on Microsoft Entra ID as their corporate IdP — it ships with M365/Azure tenants, so for many enterprises it's the default rather than a deliberate choice. Today VIP can headlessly authenticate against Keycloak, Okta, and Snowflake, but a customer on Entra falls back to interactive auth and can't exercise the full headless session-launch / API-key flows the other IdPs get.

**Docs already treat Entra as a peer of Okta.** Posit's product documentation for Workbench and Connect heavily features **both Okta and Entra/Azure AD** as the two headline enterprise SSO integrations, with dedicated OIDC/SAML configuration guides for each. Our verification tooling should reflect the same reality the docs sell: if we tell customers Entra is a fully-supported, documented integration, VIP should be able to verify a deployment authenticated through it end-to-end. Right now there's a gap between what the docs promote (Okta **and** Entra) and what VIP can headlessly test (Okta but **not** Entra).

## Current state

`src/vip/idp.py` registers strategies in `_IDP_STRATEGIES`:

```python
_IDP_STRATEGIES = {
    "keycloak": _fill_keycloak_login,
    "okta": _fill_okta_login,
    "snowflake": _fill_snowflake_login,
}
```

There is no `entra` / `azure` entry, and no Entra form-filler. `get_idp_strategy()` raises `AuthConfigError: Unsupported IdP` for Entra.

## Proposed work

- [ ] Add `_fill_entra_login(page, username, password)` modeling Entra's multi-step OIDC login flow:
  - email/UPN entry (`input[name='loginfmt']`) → **Next**
  - password entry (`input[name='passwd']`) → **Sign in**
  - the **"Stay signed in?" (KMSI)** interstitial (`#idSIButton9` / "Yes") — easy to miss, stalls the redirect if unhandled
  - optional MFA / authenticator challenge (mirror the Okta TOTP handling; honor `VIP_TEST_TOTP_SECRET`)
- [ ] Register `"entra"` in `_IDP_STRATEGIES` (consider aliasing `"azure"` / `"azuread"` → same strategy for config ergonomics).
- [ ] Verbose `_log_verbose` breadcrumbs at each hop, consistent with the Keycloak/Okta strategies.
- [ ] Extend the mock-IdP E2E coverage (see #419 / #430) to include an Entra flow where feasible, or document why Entra can't be mocked and how it's validated instead.
- [ ] Update auth docs / `vip.toml.example` to list Entra as a supported `auth_provider` IdP.

## Acceptance criteria

`vip verify --headless-auth` against a Workbench/Connect deployment fronted by Entra ID completes login (including KMSI and MFA) without interactive intervention, reaching parity with the existing Keycloak and Okta strategies.

## References

- `src/vip/idp.py` — `_IDP_STRATEGIES`, `get_idp_strategy`, existing `_fill_keycloak_login` / `_fill_okta_login`
- Related IdP/auth issues: #263, #419, #430

title: Flaky selftest: TestAutoRouting.test_small_uses_threadpool asserts failure_rate == 0.0 under load
description:
`selftests/test_load_engine.py::TestAutoRouting::test_small_uses_threadpool` runs a real 50-request load test against a local mock server and asserts `result.failure_rate == 0.0`.

On a loaded machine it intermittently observes a non-zero failure rate (e.g. `0.74`), failing the assertion. Seen locally while working on #399; not reproducible in CI.

Consider tolerating a small failure-rate threshold, or making the mock server / transport more robust under contention, so the test isn't sensitive to host load.

title: test(workbench): retire invalid R/Python version-dropdown scenarios in test_runtime_versions
description:
## Summary

The two "runtime version" scenarios in `test_runtime_versions.feature` can **only skip** on current Workbench — they can never actually execute — because they target a New Session dialog control (`#rstudio_label_r_version` / `#rstudio_label_python_version`) that no longer exists in the RStudio Pro tab. The R version selector moved *into the running IDE*, and RStudio never had a Python selector to begin with. I'm proposing we treat these two scenarios as invalid against the current UI and remove the dead selectors.

Observed skips:

```
test_runtime_versions.py::test_r_versions[chromium] SKIPPED
  (R version selector not present in New Session dialog — this Workbench instance may not expose a version dropdown)
test_runtime_versions.py::test_python_versions[chromium] SKIPPED
  (Python version selector not present in New Session dialog — this Workbench instance may not expose a version dropdown)
```

## Affected code

- Scenarios: `test_r_versions`, `test_python_versions` in `src/vip_tests/workbench/test_runtime_versions.feature` (lines 7–19) and step defs `test_runtime_versions.py:219-250`.
- Selectors: `src/vip_tests/workbench/pages/homepage.py:40-41`
  - `R_VERSION_DROPDOWN = "#rstudio_label_r_version"`
  - `PYTHON_VERSION_DROPDOWN = "#rstudio_label_python_version"`
- The `when` steps call `_read_dropdown_options()`; when the selector count is 0 they `pytest.skip(...)` with the messages above (`test_runtime_versions.py:228-233, 245-250`).

The third scenario in the file — `test_r_version_in_session` (launch RStudio, read `R.version$major` from the console) — is **unaffected** and remains a valid runtime check. This proposal is only about the two dialog-dropdown scenarios.

## Verification against a live instance

Driving the actual New Session dialog on `pwb.demo.soleng.posit.it` (Workbench **2026.07.0+139.pro9**, "Pacific Dogwood") over CDP — same instance/method used to verify the Jobs-selector fix in `2e000a63`:

- RStudio Pro tab activates; dialog title is "New Session".
- The **only** fields in the RStudio Pro tab are `#rstudio_label_session_name` and `#rstudio_label_resource_profile` (Resource Profile).
- `#rstudio_label_r_version` → **0 matches**. `#rstudio_label_python_version` → **0 matches**. No `[id*='r_version']`, no `[id*='python_version']`, no version `<select>` anywhere in the dialog.
- Expanding the "Environment" section shows only Resource Profile.
- `#workbench-cluster-advanced-options` is an **empty hidden `<div>`** — nothing behind it.
- The launched runtime ("R 4.6.1") is shown only in the session-list *Runtime* column after launch, not as a picker in the dialog.

## Why (per Posit docs)

- **R:** The R version selector is an **in-IDE** control (`#rstudio_versions_popup_menu`, top-right of a running RStudio Pro window — already modeled as `RStudioSession.R_VERSION_MENU` / `R_VERSION_MENU_ITEMS` in `pages/rstudio_session.py:23-25`). It appears only when multiple R versions are discoverable (`/etc/rstudio/r-versions`, `/opt/R/*`, profiles) and `r-versions-multiple` is not disabled. It is **not** a New Session dialog control.
  - https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/admin/r/using_multiple_versions_of_r.html
  - https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/admin/rstudio_pro_sessions/user_and_group_profiles.html#setting-r-versions-multiple
- **Python:** RStudio Pro has **no Python version selector** at all. Python/R interpreter *selection at launch* is a Workbench Jobs / VS Code / Positron Pro concept driven by the `py-versions` / `r-versions` files, not an RStudio session-dialog picker.
  - https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/admin/vscode_sessions/workbench_job_interpreters.html
  - https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/admin/positron_sessions/workbench_job_interpreters.html

The shadcn New Session dialog redesign (2026.05+) removed whatever legacy element `#rstudio_label_*_version` used to match. None of the supported versions (current + 2 back → 2026.05 / 06 / 07) render it.

## Is there any condition where they run?

- **`test_python_versions`**: No. There is no Python picker in the RStudio Pro New Session dialog by design — it will skip on every deployment.
- **`test_r_versions`**: Not with the current selector against the current dialog. It could only have passed on a pre-2026.05 build where `#rstudio_label_r_version` still rendered — outside the supported window.

## Recommendation

Treat both dialog-dropdown scenarios as invalid against current Workbench and remove the dead selectors:

1. Remove the `test_r_versions` and `test_python_versions` scenarios from `test_runtime_versions.feature` and their step defs / `_read_dropdown_options` helper from `test_runtime_versions.py`.
2. Remove `R_VERSION_DROPDOWN` / `PYTHON_VERSION_DROPDOWN` from `pages/homepage.py` (and the read paths in `start_rstudio_with_r_version` that probe `R_VERSION_DROPDOWN`).
3. Keep `test_r_version_in_session` — it validates the launched R version from the console and is the right layer for this check.

Optional follow-up (separate issue): if we want to re-assert *available* R versions, retarget at the in-IDE `RStudioSession.R_VERSION_MENU` popup after launch rather than the launch dialog. Available-Python-version coverage would belong to a Workbench Jobs / Positron / VS Code interpreter test, not RStudio.

## Context

- Feature added in #303; earlier dialog-related fixes #415 (`#modalCancelBtn` dismissal) and #416 (Positron default-IDE) are closed. This is the next layer: the dropdowns those tests read no longer exist in the dialog.

title: fix(workbench): session capacity test times out on disabled resource profiles
description:
## Summary

`test_launch_sessions_with_the_configured_resource_profile[chromium]` fails with a Playwright `TimeoutError` when a resource profile is **visible but disabled** for the authenticated user.

## Error

```
playwright._impl._errors.TimeoutError: Locator.click: Timeout 5000ms exceeded.
Call log:
  - waiting for locator("[role='option']:has-text('Large (4 CPUs, 16GB RAM)')").first
  - locator resolved to <div role="option" data-disabled="" aria-disabled="true" ...>
  - attempting click action
    - element is not enabled - retrying click action
  ...
```

## Root cause

Workbench renders resource profiles the user is **not entitled to** (e.g. a group-restricted profile) as visible `[role='option']` elements marked `aria-disabled="true"` / `data-disabled`.

In `src/vip_tests/workbench/test_session_capacity.py`:

- `_detect_profiles()` reads **every** `[role='option']`, including disabled ones, and returns them as launchable.
- `_launch_session()` then does `option.click()` on the disabled option. Playwright blocks waiting for the element to become "enabled" until the 5s timeout, and the test errors.

The scenario this exposes: *a resource profile is visible, but disabled for the currently authenticated user* — a legitimate, correctly-configured deployment state, not a product defect.

## Expected behavior

- **Auto-detected profiles:** detect all profiles but skip the disabled ones; only skip the whole scenario if *every* profile is disabled (nothing is launchable).
- **Explicitly configured profile (`workbench.session_profiles`) that is disabled:** `pytest.skip` with a clear reason naming the profile and the likely cause (group/entitlement restriction), rather than timing out.

## Affected

- `src/vip_tests/workbench/test_session_capacity.py` (`_detect_profiles`, `_launch_session`, `launch_sessions`)

title: test(workbench): session tests leave created files (Untitled*.ipynb) behind after cleanup
description:
**What happens:** The Workbench session-cleanup fixture quits/removes the *session*, but files created *inside* a session during a test — most visibly JupyterLab `Untitled*.ipynb` notebooks from `test_launch_jupyter` / `test_jupyterlab_extensions` — remain in the test account's home directory. Over many runs these accumulate (16+ observed on a live deployment).

**Why it matters:** Test litter accrues in the shared test account, and stale leftover notebooks can pop dialogs (e.g. a lingering "Error Starting Kernel" modal) that intercept clicks in later runs — a latent source of flakiness.

**Scope:** Non-destructive cleanup of VIP-created files at session/test teardown (tag or track what the test creates and remove only that; must never touch pre-existing user content). Distinct from session cleanup (#467), which is about quitting sessions, not deleting files.

**Not a blocker for #484** — surfaced during its live validation.

title: feat(workbench): run session-launch tests under --api-auth when a Workbench API token is provided
description:
## Summary

When `--api-auth` is used, **every** `@workbench` test is deselected — including tests that could run against the Workbench API with an admin/super-admin token. `--api-auth` keeps only tests marked `@api_auth`, and **no Workbench feature file carries that marker** (only the nine Connect feature files do). The plumbing to authenticate a `WorkbenchClient` with an API key already exists (`VIP_WORKBENCH_API_KEY` → `WorkbenchConfig.api_key` → `WorkbenchClient(api_key=...)`), but nothing exercises it under `--api-auth`.

This is the Workbench analog of #222 (the Connect `--no-auth`/API-key gap), which was resolved for Connect but never extended to Workbench.

## Why this matters

A common customer situation: Workbench is behind SSO that can't be scripted, and interactive/headless browser auth isn't available on the testing host, but the admin *can* mint a Workbench API token. Today VIP gives those users **zero** Workbench coverage. At minimum, an API token should let VIP verify that the relevant session types can be launched and reach an active state — the single most important Workbench capability check.

## Root cause

- `src/vip/plugin.py:509` — `_AUTH_PRODUCTS = {"connect", "workbench"}`, so every `@workbench` test is "auth-requiring".
- `src/vip/plugin.py:401` — under `--api-auth`, any auth-requiring test that is **not** `@api_auth`-marked is deselected.
- `grep -rln api_auth src/vip_tests/workbench/` → **no matches.** All session/IDE/job tests are Playwright/UI-driven (`test_ide_launch.py`, `test_session_capacity.py`, etc.), keyed off a browser storage-state session, with no API-key launch path.

So `--api-auth` + a valid `VIP_WORKBENCH_API_KEY` runs no Workbench tests at all.

## Important nuance from the Workbench API docs

I checked the official Workbench API docs. Two things the implementation must account for — the current `WorkbenchClient` does **not** match either:

1. **Auth scheme.** The Workbench API uses **API tokens as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`**, generated server-side with `rstudio-server generate-api-token <user|admin|super-admin> <name> <username>`. These are **not** Connect API keys. But `WorkbenchClient` currently sends `Authorization: Key <api_key>` (`src/vip/clients/workbench.py:48`) — Connect's scheme. An API-key launch path needs the Bearer scheme.

2. **Token privilege for launching.**
   - `user` token → launch/query/suspend/stop **own** sessions.
   - `admin` token → read metadata + stop/suspend **any** user's sessions, but **cannot launch**.
   - `super-admin` token → full access, including `launch_session` on behalf of a user.

   So a session-*launch* test via the API needs a **super-admin** (or `user`) token, not merely admin. The API is also only available on the **Enhanced/Advanced** Workbench tiers.

3. **Endpoint set.** The documented admin API is `POST /api/launch_session`, `POST /api/get_session`, `POST /api/stop_session`, `POST /api/resume_session`, `POST /api/launch_job`, `GET /api/get_compute_envs`, `GET /api/version`. The current `WorkbenchClient` instead talks to the UI-facing `/api/sessions`, `/api/sessions/{id}` (DELETE/suspend) and `/api/server/settings` endpoints, which are cookie-authenticated. Adding API-token launch coverage likely means teaching the client the documented `/api/launch_session` + `/api/get_session` methods.

Docs: https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/admin/workbench_api/workbench_api.html and https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/admin/workbench_api/interface.html

## Tests that are good candidates for an API-token path

Reviewing `src/vip_tests/workbench/`, these map cleanly onto the documented API and would be the highest-value additions:

| Test | UI scenario today | API equivalent |
|---|---|---|
| `test_ide_launch.py` | Launch RStudio / VS Code / JupyterLab / Positron | `POST /api/launch_session` (`workbench` param per IDE) + poll `get_session` for active state |
| `test_session_capacity.py` | Launch N sessions on a resource profile | repeated `launch_session` with `launch_parameters` + `get_compute_envs` to enumerate profiles/clusters |
| `test_sessions.py` | Suspend & resume | `stop_session` (suspend) + `resume_session` |
| `test_jobs.py` | Background/Workbench job runs | `launch_job` / `launch_audited_job` + `get_job_output` |
| `test_runtime_versions.py` | Expected R/Python versions available | `get_compute_envs` reports supported runtimes (partial; the "session actually uses version X" assertion may still need a session) |

Session cleanup already works over the API (`quit_vip_sessions`), so the teardown side is in place.

## Suggested direction

1. Add an `@api_auth` marker to the Workbench scenarios that can be driven purely via the API token (starting with IDE launch and session capacity).
2. Give `WorkbenchClient` a Bearer-token auth path and `launch_session`/`get_session`/`stop_session` methods, selected when an API token is configured.
3. Document that Workbench API-token testing requires a `super-admin` (or `user`) token on an Enhanced/Advanced deployment, and that `admin` tokens cannot launch sessions.
4. As with #222, `--api-auth` should then run these Workbench tests instead of deselecting the entire product.

### Key files
- `src/vip/plugin.py:401,509` — `--api-auth` deselection + `_AUTH_PRODUCTS`
- `src/vip/clients/workbench.py:48` — `Authorization: Key` header (needs a Bearer path)
- `src/vip_tests/workbench/test_ide_launch.py`, `test_session_capacity.py` — UI-only launch today
- `src/vip/config.py:266` — `VIP_WORKBENCH_API_KEY` already wired

title: fix: only recolor the progress indicator on failing lines, not every subsequent line
description:
## Summary

In `vip verify` output, once a test fails the progress-indicator coloring appears to "stick" — every subsequent line is recolored (e.g. rendered in the failure color) rather than only the line for the test that actually failed.

## Expected behavior

Only the line corresponding to a failing test should be recolored. Lines for tests that pass or skip after a failure should render in their normal color.

## Actual behavior

After the first failure, the recoloring bleeds into subsequent lines, making it look like more tests failed than actually did.

## Notes

Likely an ANSI color code that is set on a failing line but never reset, so the color persists for the rest of the run. The fix is to scope the color to the single line and reset it afterward. Likely lives in the pytest plugin / reporting output (`src/vip/plugin.py`).

title: feat: truncate test node paths in verify output unless verbose
description:
## Summary

When running `vip verify`, pytest prints the full absolute path to each test node ID. When VIP is installed as a tool (e.g. `uv tool install posit-vip`), that path is the site-packages install location, which is long and noisy:

```
../../../../.local/share/uv/tools/posit-vip/lib/python3.13/site-packages/vip_tests/prerequisites/test_components.py::test_product_server_is_reachable[Connect] PASSED [  0%]
../../../../.local/share/uv/tools/posit-vip/lib/python3.13/site-packages/vip_tests/connect/test_auth.py::test_connect_login_ui PASSED [  6%]
```

This makes the output hard to scan — the meaningful part (`connect/test_auth.py::test_connect_login_ui`) is buried behind the install prefix.

## Requested behavior

- **Default (non-verbose) run:** truncate the node path to the portion relative to `vip_tests/`, e.g. show `connect/test_auth.py::test_connect_login_ui` instead of the full site-packages path.
- **Verbose (`-v`) run:** show the full path unchanged, so the existing behavior is preserved when someone needs it for debugging.

Example of the desired default output for the line above:

```
connect/test_auth.py::test_connect_login_ui PASSED [  6%]
```

## Longer term

Each test should get a user-friendly display name that summarizes what it's doing (e.g. "Connect: admin can log in via the web UI") rather than exposing the raw pytest node ID. Truncating the path is the near-term fix; friendly names are the eventual goal.

## Notes

Likely implemented in the pytest plugin (`src/vip/plugin.py`) via a node-ID / report-header hook, gated on the pytest verbosity level.

title: fix(workbench): vip cleanup + teardown sweep quit 0 orphaned sessions (auth + UI-sweep gaps)
description:
### VIP version

0.54.1 (branch off main; **includes** the #467/#474 session-cleanup fix, commit `673ddee2`)

### Affected area

Workbench tests / `vip cleanup`

### What happened?

Orphaned Workbench sessions from VIP test runs (`VIP test_git_ops.py - gw0-...`, `VIP test_sessions.py - gw1-...`) were **not cleaned up**, and neither the in-test teardown sweep nor the `vip cleanup` CLI escape hatch (#474) could remove them. Three compounding defects, all observed live against a Workbench 2026.06 deployment (`dev.demo.posit.team`):

**1. Teardown sweep silently leaks on expired SSO.** When a test session tears down and the cached auth can no longer silently complete SSO, the UI cleanup quits nothing and only warns:
```
WARNING: UI cleanup at https://dev.demo.posit.team: could not reach an authenticated homepage
(Workbench redirected to its OIDC sign-in page and the cached session could not silently complete
SSO -- it may have expired). Quit 0 sessions.
```
Per #467's "warn, never fail" policy this is intentional non-fatal behavior — but it means orphans accumulate silently across runs (amplified badly by many iterations).

**2. `vip cleanup` reuses a stale cache instead of forcing a fresh login.** Running `vip cleanup --workbench-url https://dev.demo.posit.team` with an expired cache present:
```
WARNING: UI cleanup ...could not silently complete SSO... Quit 0 sessions.
>>> Reusing cached auth session from .../.vip-auth-cache.json
Escalating to browser-driven session cleanup ...
Quit 0 VIP Workbench session(s) via the UI
Cleanup completed successfully
```
It reuses the stale cache, silent SSO fails, and it reports success having quit 0 — never falling back to an interactive login. So the escape hatch is ineffective exactly when auth has expired. Workaround today: manually `rm .vip-auth-cache.json` first.

**3. UI sweep enumerates 0 sessions even when freshly authenticated.** After `rm .vip-auth-cache.json` and completing a fresh interactive OIDC login, with ~6 `VIP test_git_ops.py - ...` sessions clearly Active on the dashboard, the sweep still reported:
```
>>> A browser window has opened at https://dev.demo.posit.team
>>> Please log in through your identity provider.
Escalating to browser-driven session cleanup ...
Quit 0 VIP Workbench session(s) via the UI
Cleanup completed successfully
```
So the UI sweep is not matching/enumerating the VIP-named session rows on the 2026.06 "Projects / Jobs" dashboard (naming is `VIP <file> - <worker>-<ns>`; likely a row-selector or navigation-target mismatch — the sweep may not land on the session-list view, or the shadcn rows aren't enumerated).

### What did you expect to happen?

- Teardown cleanup and `vip cleanup` should remove all VIP-named orphaned sessions.
- When cached auth can't silently re-auth, `vip cleanup` should fall back to a fresh interactive (or headless-cred) login rather than reusing a stale cache and quitting 0.
- The UI sweep should enumerate and quit VIP-named sessions on the current 2026.06 dashboard.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run any Workbench git-ops test enough times that the cached SSO lapses between runs (e.g. `vip verify --workbench-url https://dev.demo.posit.team --interactive-auth -- -k clone_rstudio`, repeated).
2. Observe orphaned `VIP ...` sessions remain Active on the dashboard.
3. `vip cleanup --workbench-url https://dev.demo.posit.team` → "Quit 0" (reuses stale cache).
4. `rm .vip-auth-cache.json && vip cleanup --workbench-url https://dev.demo.posit.team`, complete the login → still "Quit 0 VIP Workbench session(s) via the UI" despite sessions present.

### Notes

Regression against #467 (PR #474). Defect (3) is the most impactful — the sweep is silently ineffective on the live 2026.06 dashboard even though CI selftests are green. Relevant code: `src/vip/workbench_ui.py` (UI sweep / `quit_vip_sessions_via_ui`, homepage reachability warning at ~`workbench_ui.py:170`), `src/vip/cli.py` `_cleanup_workbench_sessions`, `src/vip/auth.py` cached-vs-interactive auth selection. Green CI did not catch this — same class of "validate on a real deployment" gap noted throughout #467.

title: test(workbench): parallelize tests by IDE type instead of forcing serial
description:
Part of #480.

Under `--interactive-auth`/`--headless-auth`, all workbench tests authenticate as the **same shared account** and are pinned to a single xdist worker (`workbench_interactive_serial`, `conftest.py::pytest_collection_modifyitems`) to avoid a simultaneous-login storm against the OIDC IdP (which bounces sessions back to the sign-in page — the `?error=2` flakiness seen in #467 validation). The result is a fully **serial** ~10-minute run.

**Ask:** group workbench tests by IDE type (RStudio / VS Code / JupyterLab / Positron) so independent groups can run in parallel across xdist workers. This needs **per-worker authentication** (separate sessions/accounts, or staggered logins) to avoid the login storm. Deserves a short design pass on the auth-per-worker approach before implementation.

title: fix(workbench): public-repo cloning wrongly appears to require VIP_GIT_TOKEN
description:
Part of #480.

Cloning a **public** repo does not need credentials — `test_git_ops.py` already supports `auth_method="none"` (anonymous clone). A token (`VIP_GIT_TOKEN`) is only needed for `auth_method="https-token"` (push / private-repo scenarios).

But the skip message shown on a config-less run misleadingly leads with the token:

> Add a `[workbench.git_test]` block to vip.toml with clone_url and auth_method, and set VIP_GIT_TOKEN in the environment (for auth_method='https-token').

This reads as "you need a token to test git," which is false for the public/read path.

**Ask:**
1. Reword the skip so it makes clear public-repo cloning needs only `clone_url` + `auth_method="none"` (no token).
2. Ship a **default public test repo** so the anonymous clone scenarios run out-of-the-box without any config.

title: test(workbench): group git/cloning tests after session-launch tests
description:
Part of #480.

The git/cloning tests (`test_git_ops.py`) sort near the top alphabetically, so they run before the session-launch tests rather than being grouped logically after them. They also **skip entirely** unless a `[workbench.git_test]` block is present in `vip.toml`, so on a config-less `vip verify --workbench-url ...` run they never execute.

**Ask:** group the cloning tests after the session-launch tests, and make the basic (public-repo, anonymous) clone path runnable out-of-the-box (see #480 child on the git-token message + a default public repo) so they aren't silently skipped.

title: test(workbench): order tests logically (IDE launch before extensions)
description:
Part of #480.

Workbench BDD tests are collected in **default alphabetical file order**, so e.g. `test_ide_extensions.py` runs *before* `test_ide_launch.py`. There is no intentional ordering — the sequence just falls out of filenames.

Each test launches its own session (via `unique_session_name`), so nothing is functionally broken, but the order reads as arbitrary/nonsensical (extensions before launch) and makes the run hard to follow.

**Ask:** order the workbench tests intentionally (e.g. prerequisites → session launch → in-session features → extensions), via explicit ordering or a naming/collection convention, so the run tells a coherent story.

title: epic: reorganize and parallelize the Workbench test suite
description:
Tracking issue for reorganizing and (optionally) parallelizing the Workbench BDD test suite.

The suite grew organically and several structural rough edges surfaced while validating #467 (session cleanup) against a live, OIDC-fronted **Workbench 2026.06** deployment. None of these are cleanup bugs — they're test-suite organization/ergonomics.

## Sub-issues
- [x] #481 — order tests logically (IDE launch before extensions); collection is currently accidental alphabetical order
- [x] #482 — group git/cloning tests after session-launch tests (and make them runnable without config)
- [x] #483 — public-repo cloning wrongly appears to require `VIP_GIT_TOKEN` (misleading skip; add default public repo)
- [x] #479 — git-ops `push_*` tests surface a misleading "session not established" auth error when `[workbench.git_test]` is absent (skip-gate precedence); pairs with #483
- [x] #484 — parallelize tests by IDE type instead of forcing serial execution (needs per-worker auth)

## Context
- Workbench tests are collected in **default alphabetical file order** (no intentional ordering).
- Each test launches its own session, so there's no broken dependency — but the order reads as arbitrary.
- Under `--interactive-auth`/`--headless-auth` all workbench tests share **one** account and are pinned to a single xdist worker (`workbench_interactive_serial`) to avoid a simultaneous-login storm against the OIDC IdP — hence fully serial (~10 min) runs.
- git/cloning tests support anonymous public-repo clones (`auth_method="none"`) but skip entirely without a `[workbench.git_test]` config block, and the skip message misleadingly implies a token is always required.

## Suggested order of attack
1. #483 + #479 (quick win: fix the git skip gate — precedence + wording + default public repo) → also unblocks #482.
2. #481 / #482 (ordering & grouping).
3. #484 (parallelization — needs a design pass on per-worker auth).

## Not part of this epic
Launch-gate **false negatives** (#477 Positron, #478 JupyterLab) are product-test **correctness** bugs, not organization/ergonomics — tracked separately alongside #390 (which already scopes the `.positron-console` launch-gate fix).

title: fix(workbench): git-ops push_* tests report misleading 'session not established' skip when git_test config is absent
description:
### VIP version

0.54

### Affected area

Workbench tests

### What happened?

With no `[workbench.git_test]` block configured, the git-ops clone and push tests skipped for *different* reasons despite the same underlying condition:

`test_git_ops.py::test_clone_rstudio/vscode/positron` skipped correctly with:

```
Git test config is not configured. Add a [workbench.git_test] block to vip.toml with clone_url and auth_method, and set VIP_GIT_TOKEN in the environment (for auth_method='https-token').
```

But their `test_push_rstudio/vscode/positron` counterparts skipped with a misleading auth message:

```
Workbench session not established by --interactive-auth (landed on login page: https://pwb.demo.soleng.posit.it/auth-sign-in?appUri=&error=2). Next steps: rerun with --vip-verbose to see the auth flow, confirm the OIDC provider issues a session valid for Workbench's domain, and check that the Workbench auth-sign-in page does not require interaction.
```

### What did you expect to happen?

Since `git_test` config is absent, the `test_push_*` tests should skip for the **same "Git test config is not configured"** reason as the `test_clone_*` tests. Surfacing an auth-flow error here points at the wrong root cause and sends users chasing an OIDC/session problem that isn't the reason the test skipped.

### Steps to reproduce

```
vip verify --workbench-url https://pwb.demo.soleng.posit.it --interactive-auth
```

### Notes

Same class of misleading skip message as #462 — the skip reason precedence/ordering should surface the config-missing gate before the interactive-auth-session gate.

title: fix(workbench): JupyterLab tests skip (.jp-Launcher not found) though JupyterLab is installed
description:
### VIP version

0.54

### Affected area

Workbench tests

### What happened?

Both JupyterLab tests skipped claiming the IDE may not be installed:

`test_ide_launch.py::test_launch_jupyter[chromium]` and `test_ide_extensions.py::test_jupyterlab_extensions[chromium]`:

```
JupyterLab did not load within timeout — the IDE may not be installed on this Workbench instance (Locator.wait_for: Timeout 60000ms exceeded.
Call log:
  - waiting for locator(".jp-Launcher") to be visible
)
```

On this deployment JupyterLab **is** installed and launches manually, so the `.jp-Launcher` gate is producing a false negative rather than a genuine "not installed" result.

### What did you expect to happen?

The JupyterLab tests should detect the launched session and run (or fail with an accurate reason), not skip claiming JupyterLab may not be installed.

### Steps to reproduce

```
vip verify --workbench-url https://pwb.demo.soleng.posit.it --interactive-auth
```

### Notes

The `.jp-Launcher` selector may have changed across JupyterLab versions, or the launch needs a longer/alternate readiness gate. Mirrors the Positron launch-gate false-negative filed alongside this (see companion issue).

title: fix(workbench): test_launch_positron skips (.positron-console not found) though Positron is installed
description:
### VIP version

0.54

### Affected area

Workbench tests

### What happened?

`test_ide_launch.py::test_launch_positron[chromium]` skipped with:

```
Positron console element not found within timeout — selector may have changed or Positron may not be fully available (Locator.wait_for: Timeout 30000ms exceeded.
Call log:
  - waiting for locator(".positron-console") to be visible
)
```

Positron is installed and reachable on this deployment — `test_ide_extensions.py::test_positron_extensions[chromium]` PASSED in the same run — so the launch gate is producing a false negative rather than a genuine "not installed" result.

### What did you expect to happen?

`test_launch_positron` should detect the launched Positron session and run (or fail with an accurate reason), not skip claiming Positron may not be available.

### Steps to reproduce

```
vip verify --workbench-url https://pwb.demo.soleng.posit.it --interactive-auth
```

### Notes

Likely the same `.positron-console`-visibility launch gate flagged in #390 — the console element is hidden when the Terminal tab is active even though Positron loaded successfully. A more resilient gate (e.g. the Console tab `a.action-label[aria-label="Console"]`) would avoid the spurious skip. Ref #390.

title: [Feature] Update Package Manager landing page description to mention Bioconductor and OpenVSX
description: ### Affected area Package Manager tests ### What problem are you trying to solve? The homepage card for Package Manager at `website/src/pages/index.astro:26` reads "CRAN/PyPI mirrors, repository configuration, and private package access." The actual test suite covers more than that: `test_repos.feature` also verifies Bioconductor and OpenVSX mirrors, and `test_authenticated_repos.feature` verifies token-authenticated repo access, not just generic "private package access." The copy undersells what's actually verified and could lead someone to assume Bioconductor/OpenVSX/token-auth aren't covered. ### Proposed solution Update the description string to something like: "CRAN, PyPI, Bioconductor, and OpenVSX mirrors, repository configuration, and authenticated/private package access." ### Alternatives considered Leave as-is — but the description is the first thing a reader sees when deciding whether VIP already covers a given repository type, so an inaccurate summary risks duplicate manual QA effort or missed expectations.

title: Feedback: install process should not require create a venv
description:
The current install process is documented as this:

```sh
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install posit-vip
uv run vip install
vip verify --connect-url https://connect.example.com --interactive-auth
```

I propose that it would look like this:

```sh
uv tool install posit-vip
vip install
vip verify --connect-url https://connect.example.com --interactive-auth
```

Why?

- Most CLI tools that I have used to not required a venv to be created, this follows a more familiar pattern that other tools do (e.g. ruff, black, httpie, etc.)
- Tools like `uv tool install` and `pipx` provide an easy way to install Python based tooling in an isolated environment
- More simple experience. Admins who run this may not be familiar with venvs. It might be confusing why `vip` is only available after activating the `venv`. If you use `uv tool` or `pipx` the `vip` script gets installed in the users home dir and will be available on path.
- Users can more easily version the version of vip they are using (e.g. `uvx --from 'posit-vip==1.0.0' vip ...`

title: RStudio IDE tests fail on logo locator when deployed R is newer than RStudio's max-tested version
description:
## Summary

`test_launch_rstudio` and `test_workbench_job` fail waiting on the RStudio logo locator (`#rstudio_rstudio_logo`) when the Workbench host runs an **R version newer than the maximum version RStudio was tested against**. In this state RStudio emits a version-mismatch warning at session init, which appears to delay/alter the normal IDE chrome enough that the logo never becomes visible within the timeout — even though the R session itself launches and runs fine.

This is an environment condition VIP should tolerate (or report clearly), not a real product failure.

## Environment

- Posit Workbench `2026.06.0+242.pro13` (Blue Plumbago), Ubuntu 24.04
- R `4.6.1` installed and set as the session R
- Local Job Launcher, OIDC (Okta) auth, `--interactive-auth`

## Affected tests

- `src/vip_tests/workbench/test_ide_launch.py::test_launch_rstudio` — `rstudio_functional` waits on `RStudioSession.LOGO` (`test_ide_launch.py:243`, `TIMEOUT_CLEANUP`)
- `src/vip_tests/workbench/test_jobs.py::test_workbench_job` — `rstudio_ide_loaded` waits on `RStudioSession.LOGO` (`test_jobs.py:185`, `TIMEOUT_IDE_LOAD`)
- Selector: `src/vip_tests/workbench/pages/rstudio_session.py:11` → `LOGO = "#rstudio_rstudio_logo"`

Both fail with:

```
AssertionError: Locator expected to be visible
Actual value: None
Error: element(s) not found
Call log:
  - Expect "to_be_visible" with timeout 60000ms
  - waiting for locator("#rstudio_rstudio_logo")
```

`test_launch_vscode` **passes** in the same run and Positron/JupyterLab sessions spawn, so auth and the launcher are healthy — this is specific to the classic RStudio IDE chrome.

## Root cause evidence

The per-user `rsession` log shows the version warning firing on every RStudio init:

```
[rsession-<user>] WARNING R version 4.6.1 is newer than the maximum version of R
tested with this version of RStudio (4.6.0). If you experience issues, please try
updating RStudio to a newer version.
LOGGED FROM: rInit(...) src/cpp/session/SessionMain.cpp:608
```

The session process tree confirms sessions actually start and run (RStudio `rsession`, Positron `ark` kernel, `code-server` all live). So the R session is functional; only the logo assertion times out.

## Suggested handling (any of)

1. When the RStudio "newer than max tested R version" warning/interstitial is present, dismiss it (or wait past it) before asserting on `RStudioSession.LOGO`.
2. Broaden the readiness check to an element that is present regardless of the warning banner (e.g. the RStudio workbench pane container) rather than only the logo.
3. If the logo genuinely never renders in this state, downgrade to a clear skip/xfail with a message naming the R-vs-RStudio version mismatch, so operators aren't chasing a false failure.

## Repro

Deploy Workbench with an R version one minor line ahead of the RStudio build's max-tested R (here R 4.6.1 vs RStudio max-tested 4.6.0), then run:

```
vip verify --workbench-url https://<host> --interactive-auth
```

title: fix(ssl): TLS-version scenario fails and redirect-step error handling inconsistent under insecure/self-signed
description:
Two independent quirks in `src/vip_tests/cross_product/test_ssl.py`, surfaced while validating #455 (PR #455) locally against a self-signed HTTPS server with `tls.insecure = true`. Neither blocked #455 (which correctly makes the http-only / insecure cases skip), but both are worth fixing.

## 1. TLS-version scenario fails on self-signed + `insecure=true` with misdirected guidance

With a self-signed cert and `tls.insecure = true`, `test_tls_12_or_higher_is_enforced_for_product` **fails**:

```
TLS 1.2 handshake reached the server, but the test runner could not verify the
server's certificate. This is a certificate-trust issue on the runner... set
SSL_CERT_FILE to a CA bundle... Detail: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED]
certificate verify failed: self-signed certificate
```

`_attempt_tls` (`test_ssl.py`) always builds an `ssl.create_default_context()` with `check_hostname=True` / `verify_mode=CERT_REQUIRED`, so a self-signed cert yields `cert_verify_failed` even though the user explicitly set `insecure=true`. The scenario is about **TLS-version enforcement**, not certificate validity, so on an `insecure` run it should still be able to assess which TLS versions the server accepts. The `_attempt_tls` path could relax cert verification when `vip_config.insecure` is set (still reporting `connected` vs `rejected` per version), so the version check remains meaningful instead of failing on a trust error the user opted out of. The "set SSL_CERT_FILE" hint is also misdirected in this case — the user didn't misconfigure trust, they disabled it.

## 2. Redirect-step error handling inconsistent with the sibling HTTPS step

`request_http` (`test_ssl.py`) and `make_http_request` (`src/vip_tests/security/test_https.py`) both probe the HTTP URL, but classify a connection/protocol error differently:

- `test_https.py::make_http_request` treats **any** exception (incl. `httpx.ConnectError`) as `refused: True` → the "connection is refused or redirected" assertion passes (HTTP port closed is acceptable).
- `test_ssl.py::request_http` only special-cases `httpx.ConnectError` as `port_closed`; other transport errors fall through to a generic `error` string, and an HTTP request that lands on a TLS-only port raises a protocol error that isn't classified as `port_closed` → the redirect assertion can fail instead of treating "no plain-HTTP listener" as acceptable.

The two sibling steps should classify "no usable plain-HTTP endpoint" consistently. Align `request_http`'s handling with `make_http_request` (treat a broader set of transport/protocol errors as "port closed / not enforcing over HTTP is N/A").

## Repro

Self-signed HTTPS server on `127.0.0.1:8443`, `vip.toml` with `[connect] url = "https://127.0.0.1:8443"` and `[tls] insecure = true`, then:

```
uv run vip verify --config <toml> --categories cross-product -- -k "ssl" -v
```

Observed: `test_ssl_certificate_is_valid_for_product` SKIPPED (correct, #455), but `test_tls_12_or_higher_is_enforced_for_product` and `test_http_redirects_to_https_for_product` FAILED.

title: terminal_run swallows real command errors as a generic 120s timeout
description:
## Summary

`terminal_run` (`src/vip_tests/workbench/exec.py`) cannot distinguish "the command failed immediately" from "the command is still running," so any command that exits non-zero is reported as a generic timeout after the full wait period, with the real error message discarded.

## Root cause

```python
done_marker = f"VIP_DONE_{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
tmpfile = f"/tmp/vip_term_{uuid.uuid4().hex}.txt"
shell_cmd = f'{cmd} > {tmpfile} 2>&1 && echo "{done_marker}" >> {tmpfile}'
```

The done-marker is only appended via `&&`, i.e. only if `cmd` exits 0. When `cmd` fails fast, the marker is never written to `tmpfile`, so the polling loop in `terminal_run` has no way to detect completion — it keeps polling until `timeout` elapses and then raises:

```
ExecError: terminal_run timed out after 120000ms waiting for done marker in '/tmp/vip_term_....txt'
```

This is misleading (it reads like a hang) and throws away the actual command output, which is sitting untouched in `tmpfile` the whole time (e.g. a `git clone` failure like `fatal: destination path '...' already exists...` — see #438). It affects every caller of `terminal_run`, not just the git-ops tests, and turns every real, fast failure into a slow, uninformative one — which also inflates test run time (each swallowed failure burns its full configured timeout, e.g. 120s for git network operations).

## Suggested fix

Write the marker unconditionally (`;` instead of `&&`), and capture the exit code alongside it:

```python
shell_cmd = f'{cmd} > {tmpfile} 2>&1; echo "{done_marker}:$?" >> {tmpfile}'
```

Then, once the marker line is found, parse the trailing exit code and raise `ExecError` immediately with the captured output when it's non-zero, instead of returning/looping as if nothing happened. This turns a 120-second uninformative timeout into an immediate, actionable error for every `terminal_run` caller.

title: Workbench git-ops clone scenarios fail with 'destination path already exists' on reused QA VMs
description:
## Summary

Every "Clone a Git repository in `<IDE>` terminal" scenario in `test_git_ops.py` clones into the same fixed, deterministic path — `/tmp/jumpstart_examples` — and nothing ever removes it afterward. On the long-lived Workbench QA VMs (not redeployed per `vip verify` run, and Workbench scenarios run serially against one VM via `-n 0`), this causes `git clone` to fail with:

```
fatal: destination path 'jumpstart_examples' already exists and is not an empty directory.
```

...as soon as any prior clone (a different IDE scenario in the same run, or a previous day's run) leaves the directory behind.

## Root cause

`_do_clone` (`src/vip_tests/workbench/test_git_ops.py`):

```python
def _do_clone(page, git_session_ctx, git_cfg, readback_lang, *, workdir="/tmp"):
    auth_url = _inject_token_into_url(git_cfg.clone_url, git_cfg.token)
    repo_dir = _repo_dir_from_url(git_cfg.clone_url)
    clone_dir = f"{workdir}/{repo_dir}"

    terminal_run(
        page,
        f"cd {shlex.quote(workdir)} && GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git clone {shlex.quote(auth_url)}",
        ...
    )
```

- `clone_dir` is always `/tmp/jumpstart_examples` — identical across the RStudio, VS Code, and Positron clone scenarios, and across every future run against the same VM.
- There is a `_wb_git_cleanup_state` fixture that cleans up *remote* pushed branches after push scenarios, but nothing analogous cleans up the *local* clone directory after any scenario (clone-only or push).
- Once one scenario successfully clones, every subsequent clone attempt (same run, different IDE; or a future verify run on the same persistent VM) fails with the "already exists" error above.

Observed in practice: a `workbench-lm-gcp` QA verify run failed `test_clone_rstudio` and `test_clone_vscode` with this error; the same error text was also present in other Workbench instances' logs (their VMs have the same stale leftover from earlier runs, it just hadn't caused a *reported* failure in that run).

Related: the failure is reported as a 120s `ExecError` timeout rather than surfacing the actual git error — that's tracked separately in #439 since it affects `terminal_run` generally, not just this test.

## Suggested fix

In `_do_clone`, defensively remove any pre-existing destination before cloning, e.g.:

```python
f"rm -rf {shlex.quote(clone_dir)} && cd {shlex.quote(workdir)} && "
f"GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git clone {shlex.quote(auth_url)}"
```

This makes each clone scenario self-contained regardless of what a prior IDE scenario or a prior verify run left behind, without needing to plumb unique per-scenario directory names through the branch/commit/push/delete steps that already reference `git_session_ctx["clone_dir"]`.

title: [Feature] Auto-recompile gh-aw lockfiles on Dependabot actions PRs
description:
## Problem
Dependabot's weekly **actions** bump edits the shared actions pinned inside the gh-aw compiled `.lock.yml` files (checkout, setup-uv, upload/download-artifact, github-script, setup-node, setup-just). Those pins are owned by the gh-aw compiler, not dependabot, so the bump leaves the lockfiles stale and the **Agentic Workflow Lockfile Guard** (ci.yml) fails on the dependabot PR (e.g. #429).

Neither simple mitigation is safe:
- **Dependabot ignore-list** for those actions would freeze bumps for nearly every action the repo uses (they're all used in hand-written workflows too).
- **Exempting dependabot from the guard** turns the PR green, but if merged with its `.lock.yml` hunks, `gh aw compile` reverts them on the next PR → the guard then fails repo-wide until a manual recompile.

## Proposed fix
Add a workflow that, on a Dependabot **actions** PR, runs `gh aw compile` and pushes the recompiled `.lock.yml` files back to the Dependabot branch so they match the compiler again.

Requires a token that can push to Dependabot PR branches — Dependabot's `GITHUB_TOKEN` is read-only, so this needs a GitHub App token or PAT (maintainer/@statik to provision).

## Notes
- The guard is (currently) not a required check, so #429-style failures are red-X noise, not merge blockers — this is a hygiene/robustness fix, not urgent.
- Related: #425 (robust dependency audit), #409 (robust CI/CD epic). Companion to #433 (skips example-report on dependabot PRs).

title: [Feature] Automate --interactive-auth E2E against mock IdP
description:

The mock-IdP E2E suite covers `--headless-auth` end-to-end against a seeded Keycloak realm. `--interactive-auth` E2E automation was deferred: `start_interactive_auth()` has no form-filling — it waits for a human to click through the IdP — so automating it in CI requires driving a second browser process via CDP concurrently with the blocked `vip verify` call. title: [Feature] Robust dependency audit + deterministic lockfile handling
description:
Child of #409 (robust CI/CD epic). **Doing now — unblocks current PRs; independent of #411.**

## Problem
The Dependency Audit job (`uv sync --all-extras` + `pip-audit --skip-editable`) runs on every PR/push against the **live** advisory DB across the **full** tree (incl. dev/load/report tooling — 206 pkgs). A new CVE disclosure turns every open PR *and* main red at once, unrelated to the diff. This drives:
- a reactive floor-pin treadmill (#123, #135, #212, #216, #234, #243, #249, #256, #278, #392, #424), and
- constant `uv.lock` merge conflicts as concurrent PRs (amplified by the agentic workflows) race the lockfile against a fast-moving main.

## Fix
1. **Scope + schedule the audit.** PR-time audit covers only shipped runtime deps (`uv export` without extras — 66 pkgs vs 206) and is non-blocking/informational. A new scheduled workflow runs the full `--all-extras` audit daily on main and opens a deduped issue when a new vuln appears.
2. **Lean on existing Dependabot.** Security updates are already enabled (verified `vulnerability-alerts` = 204). Rely on it for remediation; stop hand-pinning transitive CVEs.
3. **Deterministic lockfile handling.** Pin the uv version used for locking (fixes the upload-time churn) + a `just relock` / `resolve-lock` recipe + docs, so `uv.lock` conflicts resolve deterministically.

## Acceptance
- A new CVE disclosure no longer breaks unrelated PRs.
- Scheduled audit opens/updates an issue on new vulns (does not block PRs).
- Documented, deterministic `uv.lock` conflict resolution; pinned uv lock version.


## Tracking
- [x] Part 1 — scope PR audit to runtime deps + scheduled full-tree audit (#426)
- [x] Part 2 — pin the uv version used for locking + `just relock` recipe + docs for deterministic `uv.lock` conflict resolution

title: [Feature] Release/publish hardening for 1.0
description:
Child of #409 (robust CI/CD epic).

Harden the release and publish pipeline for 1.0: `release.yml`, `publish.yml`, `docker.yml`.

Scope was narrowed during planning (`thoughts/shared/plans/2026-07-23-issue-409-finish-cicd-epic.md`, Track C): container-image cosign/provenance is out of scope, and 1.0 cutover automation is deferred in favour of a documented manual cut.

## Delivered

- `publish.yml` asserts the pushed tag matches the `pyproject` version before anything is built, and the release job is gated on that assertion, so a mistagged tag never publishes.
- PyPI upload runs through `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` with `attestations: true` — PEP 740 attestations signed via Sigstore, under trusted publishing.
- The GitHub release is owned end to end by `publish.yml` (semantic-release runs `--no-vcs-release`): release notes are cut from `CHANGELOG.md`, the locked `constraints-<version>.txt` is attached while the release is still a draft, its presence is verified, and only then is the release published and locked by immutable releases. The step is idempotent, so a partial failure can be re-run.
- The published package is smoke-tested: `smoke-published` installs `posit-vip==<version>` from public PyPI with an indexing retry loop and asserts `vip --version` reports the released version.
- `docker.yml` pulls and runs the pushed image on tag builds.
- 1.0 version-bump correctness is settled and documented in `docs/development.md` ("Versioning and the 1.0 cutover"): `major_on_zero = false` is intentional so the pipeline can never auto-cut 1.0, and shipping 1.0 is a deliberate, reviewed, manual PR.

## Remaining

- [ ] Attest the release artifacts. Neither the `uv build` wheel/sdist nor `constraints-<version>.txt` carries a GitHub attestation today. The PyPI attestations only protect the PyPI download path; anyone consuming a GitHub release asset has nothing to verify against. Adds `actions/attest-build-provenance` in the job that produces each artifact, verifiable with `gh attestation verify <file> --repo posit-dev/vip`.

## Out of scope (by decision)

- Container-image cosign / SLSA provenance / SBOM. `docker/build-push-action` runs without `provenance:` or `sbom:`, and the GHCR digest is unsigned. This is a known, accepted gap — reopen as its own issue if the image becomes a distribution channel rather than a CI convenience.
- Automating the 0.x to 1.0.0 transition. The manual path is documented; a `workflow_dispatch` forced bump was considered and rejected as an unnecessary footgun.

## Acceptance

title: [Feature] Promote smoke workflows to gated product integration runs
description:
Child of #409 (robust CI/CD epic).

Promote the smoke workflows (`connect-smoke.yml`, `workbench-smoke.yml`, `packagemanager-smoke.yml`, `connect-integration.yml`) from `--collect-only` dry runs into **gated integration runs** against containerized Connect / Workbench / Package Manager.

## Delivered

- All three product smoke workflows start the product in a container and run real `pytest` suites — no `--collect-only` anywhere in them.
- Each has an always-run `… Status` aggregator job, and all three (`Connect Smoke Tests Status`, `Workbench Smoke Tests Status`, `Package Manager Smoke Tests Status`) are required status checks on `main`.
- The green-check-with-zero-coverage hole is closed: `packagemanager-smoke.yml` fails loudly when `RSPM_LICENSE` is missing instead of skipping every step, and each Status job treats "in scope for this PR but not success" as a hard gate failure rather than a clean skip.
- The only surviving `--collect-only` is the collection guard in `ci.yml`. That one stays: it catches import and collection errors cheaply on PRs that do not warrant a full product run, and it no longer stands in for real execution.

## Remaining

- [ ] Promote `connect-integration.yml`. It runs `vip verify --api-auth --categories connect` against a real Connect container, but only on `push` / `schedule` / `workflow_dispatch`, with no Status job and no required check. Either give it the aggregator + required-check treatment, or record in the workflow why it stays scheduled-only (runtime is the likely reason).
- [ ] Close the required-check gaps in `ci.yml`. `Type Check`, `Actions Lint (zizmor)`, `Dependency Audit` and `Lockfile Guard` are not required checks, so a failure in any of them does not block merge. All four are conditional on the `changes` job, so they need the same aggregator pattern as `Selftests Status` before they can be required — a failed `changes` job must not be able to satisfy the gate by skipping its dependents.
- [ ] Add `Mock-IdP E2E Status` (from #419) to the required-check set. The job and its aggregator already exist; only the ruleset entry is missing.

## Split out

Broader product-suite coverage is now tracked separately, as children of #409:

- #539 — expand Workbench smoke to the full Workbench suite (5 of 14 test files run today)
- #540 — run the cross-product / security / config-hygiene suites against containerized products

## Acceptance

- Every product-integration workflow that gates merges reports through an always-run Status job that cannot pass while its tests were skipped or its scoping job failed.
- The required-check set on `main` covers CI's static-analysis and lockfile jobs and the mock-IdP E2E suite, not only lint, selftests and the three product smokes.

title: [Bug] test_r_version_in_session launches default IDE (Positron), times out on #rstudio_container
description:
### VIP version

0.49.2 (also present on `main` @ `v0.49.2-2-g10d64772`)

### Affected area

Workbench tests

### What happened?

`vip_tests/workbench/test_runtime_versions.py::test_r_version_in_session` fails with a 60s timeout waiting for `#rstudio_container`.

Root cause: the step `start_rstudio_with_r_version` (`test_runtime_versions.py:262`) sets `session_context["ide_type"] = "RStudio"` and fills the R version, session name, and clicks **Launch**, but it **never selects the RStudio IDE tab** in the New Session dialog. As a result the dialog launches its *default* IDE — which on current Workbench is **Positron**, not RStudio. The test then waits for `RStudioSession.CONTAINER = "#rstudio_container"`, which never appears in a Positron session.

The captured accessibility tree at failure confirms a Positron session launched ("Welcome - Positron", Positron R 4.6.0 console), not RStudio:

```
test_r_version_in_session[chromium]: Locator expected to be visible
Actual value: - application: - text: Welcome - Positron ...
Error: element(s) not found
Call log:
  - Expect "to_be_visible" with timeout 60000ms
  - waiting for locator("#rstudio_container")
```

Reproduced on every environment in the matrix — Workbench BYOL on AWS/Azure/GCP and Workbench LM on Azure/GCP — so it is deterministic, not flaky.

Contrast: `test_ide_launch.py::_start_session` (lines 154–198) **does** select the IDE tab via `dialog.get_by_role("tab", name=ide_display)` + `ide_tab.click()` before launching, and `test_launch_rstudio` passes. `start_rstudio_with_r_version` is missing that tab-selection step.

### What did you expect to happen?

The test should explicitly select the RStudio (Pro) IDE tab in the New Session dialog so that an RStudio session is launched, then assert the R version inside that RStudio session.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy a current Workbench instance whose New Session dialog defaults to Positron.
2. Set `[runtimes]` expected R versions in `vip.toml`.
3. Run `uv run vip verify` (Workbench subset).
4. `test_r_version_in_session` launches Positron and times out after 60s waiting for `#rstudio_container`.

### Relevant logs or output

```shell
FAILED workbench/test_runtime_versions.py::test_r_version_in_session[chromium]
# Expect "to_be_visible" timeout 60000ms waiting for locator("#rstudio_container")
# Actual DOM shows a Positron session ("Welcome - Positron")
```

### Suggested fix

In `start_rstudio_with_r_version`, select the RStudio IDE tab before launching, mirroring `_start_session` in `test_ide_launch.py`:

```python
ide_display = NewSessionDialog.ide_display_name("RStudio")  # -> "RStudio Pro"
ide_tab = dialog.get_by_role("tab", name=ide_display)
if ide_tab.count() == 0:
    # skip gracefully — RStudio not available on this deployment
    ...
ide_tab.click(timeout=TIMEOUT_QUICK)
# then read/select the R version dropdown, fill name, wait for Launch, click Launch
```

This guarantees the launched session is RStudio (matching the `#rstudio_container` assertion) rather than the dialog's default IDE.

### Environment

- vip 0.49.2, Python 3.14 (uv tool install)
- Products under test: Posit Workbench (BYOL and LM) on AWS, Azure, GCP
- Discovered via Posit marketplace image QA (`just verify workbench`)

title: [Bug] test_runtime_versions: R/Python version checks fail dismissing dialog via #modalCancelBtn
description:
### VIP version

0.49.2 (also present on `main` @ `v0.49.2-2-g10d64772`)

### Affected area

Workbench tests

### What happened?

`vip_tests/workbench/test_runtime_versions.py::test_r_versions` and `::test_python_versions` fail while **dismissing** the New Session dialog. After opening the dialog and reading the version dropdown, both steps call `page.locator(NewSessionDialog.CANCEL_BUTTON).click(...)`, where `CANCEL_BUTTON = "#modalCancelBtn"` (`workbench/pages/homepage.py:15`). That element is not actionable in the current Workbench New Session dialog, so the click times out.

```
test_r_versions[chromium]: an unexpected error occurred:
playwright._impl._errors.TimeoutError: Locator.click: Timeout 5000ms exceeded.
Call log:
  - waiting for locator("#modalCancelBtn")
```

This reproduced on **every** environment in the matrix — Workbench BYOL on AWS/Azure/GCP and Workbench LM on Azure/GCP — i.e. it is deterministic and product-version-independent, not a flaky/instance issue.

Notably, the project already knows `#modalCancelBtn` is unreliable: `test_ide_launch.py` introduced `_dismiss_dialog_and_skip()` (lines 201–221), which wraps the cancel click in `try/except (PlaywrightTimeoutError, PlaywrightError)` precisely to avoid "a 30-second Playwright default-timeout error on `#modalCancelBtn`". `test_runtime_versions.py` was never updated to use that defensive dismiss and still calls the cancel button directly with a hard timeout.

### What did you expect to happen?

The version-availability checks should read the R/Python options from the New Session dialog and then close the dialog cleanly (or skip gracefully if the selector is absent), without the dialog-dismiss step itself failing the test.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy a current Workbench instance (rstudio-pro New Session dialog).
2. Configure `[runtimes]` expected R/Python versions in `vip.toml`.
3. Run `uv run vip verify` (or the Workbench subset) against it.
4. `test_r_versions` and `test_python_versions` fail on the `#modalCancelBtn` click.

### Relevant logs or output

```shell
===== 3 failed, 12 passed, 23 skipped, 91 deselected =====
FAILED workbench/test_runtime_versions.py::test_r_versions[chromium]
FAILED workbench/test_runtime_versions.py::test_python_versions[chromium]
# both: TimeoutError waiting for locator("#modalCancelBtn")
```

### Suggested fix

Replace the two direct `CANCEL_BUTTON.click()` calls in `check_r_versions_in_dialog` / `check_python_versions_in_dialog` with a best-effort dismiss (e.g. reuse/extract the `_dismiss_dialog_and_skip` pattern, or press `Escape`), so closing the dialog is resilient to the `#modalCancelBtn` selector being absent/non-actionable. The version-presence assertions are the point of these tests; dialog teardown should not be able to fail them.

### Environment

- vip 0.49.2, Python 3.14 (uv tool install)
- Products under test: Posit Workbench (BYOL and LM) on AWS, Azure, GCP
- Discovered via Posit marketplace image QA (`just verify workbench`)

title: Remove Shiny and Kubernetes modes
description:
## Decision

Hard-delete both the Shiny app mode (`vip app`) and the Kubernetes execution mode (`--k8s`) in a single PR. VIP becomes a purely local CLI — supply a `vip.toml` (or `--connect-url`/`--workbench-url`/`--pm-url`) and run against reachable URLs. Pre-1.0, no deprecation. Not out of scope for the future; just not a 1.0 priority.

## Remove

**Kubernetes mode:** `Mode.k8s_job` + `Mode.config_only` (`config.py`), `--k8s`/`--config-only` flags + `cluster connect` (`cli.py`), all of `src/vip/cluster/`, all of `src/vip/verify/` (site/credentials/job), the `_run_k8s_job`/`_phase_provision_credentials` paths + the `cleanup_credentials` branch in `cleanup`.

**Shiny mode:** `app` subcommand + `run_app`, all of `src/vip/app/`, `shiny[theme]` (+ orphaned `python-multipart`/`starlette` pins) from `pyproject.toml`, shiny-only code in `report_html.py`.

## Keep (explicit)

`verify`, `cleanup`, `install`/`uninstall`, `report`, `status`, `scaffold`, `auth mint-connect-key`, CLI-flag config generation, and **all Shiny *product tests*** (deploying Shiny to Connect — unrelated to "Shiny mode").

## Do NOT delete

The root `Dockerfile` — it's a generic VIP test-runner image that #409 will repurpose for CI. Just drop the "Kubernetes Jobs" framing from its comment.

## Acceptance

Selftests pass · `vip --help` shows no `app`/`cluster` and no `--k8s`/`--config-only` · ruff + mypy clean · no dangling imports · docs updated (`README.md`, delete `docs/shiny-app.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) · `shiny` gone from deps · showboat demo.

title: [Feature] Better version gating
description:
Improve version gating beyond today's skip-only `@pytest.mark.min_version`.

**In scope:** behavior/selector switching per version · robust version parsing · unknown-version handling · "N/A" report status. **Out:** `max_version`/ranges (deprioritized).

**Mechanism:** VIP already separates selectors into `pages/` classes — add a **version dimension** via **versioned page-object subclasses + cumulative inheritance** (`Homepage` → `Homepage_2026_05`, each holding only the delta), selected by a `get_<page>(version)` factory. Behavior flows use an `idp.py`-style strategy dict keyed by version range. Support window: current + 1–2 back.

**Parser:** replace `plugin.py:_version_tuple` with a real Posit calendar-version type (`YYYY.MM.patch` + `-dev`/`-daily`/`+build`).

**Unknown version:** skip + N/A + warn. **Report:** distinct "N/A (version)" status.

**Depends on #411.** Feeds #409 Child B.
