title: fix(workbench): Positron git-ops readback times out (console proven in isolation)
description:
The Positron **console readback mechanism is proven in isolation**: a probe wrote a file via the terminal and read it back through the console (`.console-instance[style*="z-index: auto"]` / `.console-input` / `div span`, after the interpreter is input-ready) — PASS. But the **git-ops `clone_positron`/`push_positron` flow times out**:

```
ExecError: terminal_run timed out after 840000ms waiting for done marker in '/tmp/vip_term_*.txt'
```

The `DONE` marker never appears in the temp file within the poll window.

## Likely causes to investigate (live, ~20 min/iteration)
- The `git clone` may not actually execute in Positron's terminal (so the temp file / `DONE` marker is never written).
- The poll loop's repeated Console-tab activation + re-typing of `cat(readLines(...))` may interfere with the running terminal command.
- The clone may fail (auth/token/path), so `&& echo DONE` short-circuits and `DONE` is never appended.

## Launch gate
`launch_positron` currently gates on `.positron-console` being **visible**, which spuriously SKIPS whenever the Terminal tab is active (Positron loaded, console hidden). A Console-tab gate (`PositronSession.CONSOLE_TAB = 'a.action-label[aria-label="Console"]'`) is more correct, but it exposes the readback timeout above (turns a graceful skip into a failure). Reintroduce the Console-tab gate **together** with the integration fix.

## Context
- Sibling fix #386 reworked the readback: RStudio (R console), Positron (console eval — proven here in isolation), VS Code (editor-open — **validated end-to-end** in git-ops).
- `positron_eval_r`/`positron_eval_python` already activate the Console tab (`exec._activate_positron_console`); the remaining gap is the end-to-end clone+readback integration.
- Related: slow Positron session/console cold-start (#388).

title: workbench session cold-start exceeds default timeout on slow deployments
description:
**Discovered during live validation.** On staging, Workbench session cold-start regularly exceeds the default `TIMEOUT_SESSION_START` (90s) — sometimes >360s. Sessions only reached Active with `VIP_TIMEOUT_SCALE=3–5` (validated working — #368).

The tests are correct; the default is just too tight for slow/cold deployments.

## Options

- Raise the default `TIMEOUT_SESSION_START`, and/or
- Document `VIP_TIMEOUT_SCALE` prominently as the knob for slow environments.

title: fix(workbench): session cleanup silently fails (cookie auth + stale SESSION_LIST selector)
description:
**Discovered during live validation** on `dev.academy.staging.posit.team`. VIP test sessions accumulate because teardown silently no-ops.

## Two defects

1. **Cookie auth doesn't authenticate `/api/sessions`.** `_quit_vip_sessions_via_cookies` (`src/vip_tests/workbench/conftest.py:339`) → `quit_vip_sessions` (`src/vip/clients/workbench.py:95`) calls `GET /api/sessions` with browser cookies, which this Workbench rejects → no sessions listed → nothing quit.
2. **Stale selector.** `Homepage.SESSION_LIST = "#sessionsList"` (`src/vip_tests/workbench/pages/homepage.py:106`) does not match this Workbench version's markup; `tbody tr` works.

Net: leaked `VIP test*` sessions pile up. A manual UI sweep was used as a stopgap during validation.

title: fix(workbench): #363 git-ops readback only works for RStudio (VS Code + Positron time out)
description:
**Discovered during live validation** of the 2026-06-11/12 merge wave against `dev.academy.staging.posit.team` (Workbench, SSO). #363 git-ops passes for RStudio (`clone_rstudio`/`push_rstudio`) but **all VS Code and Positron scenarios fail with a 120s `terminal_run` timeout**.

## Root cause

`terminal_run` (`src/vip_tests/workbench/exec.py:373`) polls for its done-marker via `read_file(..., lang=readback_lang)`. The readback routing is incomplete for non-RStudio IDEs:

- **VS Code** (`readback_lang="python"`): `read_file` → `vscode_eval` (`exec.py:302`), which blocks on `expect(REPL_INPUT).to_be_visible()` — the Python *Interactive Window*. A fresh VS Code session never opens it, so every poll raises and `terminal_run` times out.
- **Positron**: `read_file`/`file_exists` (`exec.py:439`, `exec.py:463`) branch only `lang=="r"`→`rstudio_eval` else→`vscode_eval`. There is **no Positron branch**, even though `positron_eval_r`/`positron_eval_python` exist (`exec.py:195`, `exec.py:227`). Positron's console matches neither selector set → timeout.

## Evidence

- `test_clone_vscode` / `test_push_vscode` FAILED with `terminal_run timed out after 120000ms waiting for done marker`.
- `test_clone_positron` FAILED with the same timeout.

The terminal itself opens fine — #385 already fixed terminal-open; this is purely the readback path.

## Fix options

- **Positron**: add `positron_eval_r`/`positron_eval_python` routing in `read_file`/`file_exists`.
- **VS Code**: open/ensure the Interactive Window before `vscode_eval`, or perform marker readback through a terminal-native path instead of the REPL.

Until fixed, #363 is validated for **RStudio only**.

title: vip status: add machine-readable (JSON) output for headless consumers
description:
**What:** A machine-readable output mode for `vip status` (e.g. `--output json` / `--json`), emitting per-product results — name, configured/enabled, URL, HTTP status, and ok/fail/skip state — plus an overall status, alongside the existing 0/1 exit code.

**Why:** `vip verify --report <path>` already writes a parseable `results.json`, which makes it easy to consume verification results programmatically. `vip status` currently prints only human-formatted text plus an exit code (`src/vip/cli.py::run_status`), so automated/headless callers can't consume the quick health check per-product without scraping stdout. A small JSON contract would give the quick check the same programmatic parity that `vip verify` already offers.

**Nice-to-have:** keep the schema aligned with `reporting.py::load_results` field names (`products`, `outcome`, etc.) so consumers can share one model across `status` and `verify`.

title: test(workbench): add RStudio Git-pane commit/push scenario (validated against live Workbench)
description:
## Context

PR #363 (Git operations from Workbench sessions, closes #306) originally included a *"Commit and push using the RStudio Git pane"* scenario plus a `RStudioGitPane` page object. It was **dropped before merge** because:

1. The selectors in `RStudioGitPane` were never validated against a live Workbench instance (the code carried a TODO note to that effect).
2. The working-directory setup used `Rscript -e 'setwd(...)'` run in the terminal, which spawns a *separate* R process and does **not** change the already-running RStudio session's working directory — so the Git pane would never discover the cloned repo.

The terminal-based Git scenarios (RStudio/VSCode/Positron clone + branch/commit/push) shipped in #363 and work.

## What's needed

- Re-add the RStudio Git-pane GUI scenario, with selectors verified against a live Workbench (e.g. ganso01-staging).
- Set the session working directory via `rstudio_eval(page, 'setwd(...)')` (in-session), not a terminal `Rscript` subprocess.
- Re-introduce a validated `RStudioGitPane` page object.

## References
- PR #363
- Original feature issue #306

title: test_workbench_login fails with "You must enter a username" under interactive auth
description:
## Summary

`test_workbench_login[chromium]` fails with `Login failed: You must enter a username` when a customer runs VIP with `--interactive-auth` (or `--headless-auth`) and does not provide `VIP_TEST_USERNAME` / `VIP_TEST_PASSWORD`.

Reported by a customer via Lisa Anders (2026-06-09).

## Root cause

`src/vip_tests/workbench/test_auth.py` is a password-form-only test. Its local `page` fixture strips `storage_state` so the login form is genuinely exercised, even when `--interactive-auth` has pre-authenticated the rest of the suite.

The `workbench_accessible` step at `src/vip_tests/workbench/test_auth.py:43` skips when `auth_provider != "password"`, but it does **not** skip when:

- `auth_provider == "password"` (the default), AND
- the user is relying on `--interactive-auth` / `--headless-auth` instead of `VIP_TEST_USERNAME` / `VIP_TEST_PASSWORD`

In that configuration, `workbench_login` (`src/vip_tests/workbench/conftest.py:201`) is called with an empty `test_username`, fills the empty field, submits, and Workbench rejects the form with `You must enter a username`. This bubbles up through the retry loop at `conftest.py:283-324`.

## Expected behavior

When the user authenticated via `--interactive-auth` / `--headless-auth` and no test username/password is configured, `test_workbench_login` should skip with a clear message — the password login form cannot be exercised without credentials.

## Fix sketch

In `workbench_accessible` (or the local `page` fixture) at `src/vip_tests/workbench/test_auth.py`:

- Skip when `interactive_auth` is True regardless of `auth_provider`, OR
- Skip when `test_username` / `test_password` are empty

The first is simpler and matches the intent: this test exists to validate the password form flow, which is incompatible with pre-loaded auth sessions.

## Repro

1. Configure `vip.toml` with `auth.provider = "password"` (or omit) and no `VIP_TEST_USERNAME` / `VIP_TEST_PASSWORD` env vars
2. Run `uv run vip verify --interactive-auth --categories workbench`
3. Observe `test_workbench_login[chromium]` fails with `Login failed: You must enter a username`

## Related

Customer report also surfaced two job-test failures tracked separately.

<summary>What is a Detection Problem?</summary>

A detection problem occurs when the threat detection system either:
- **Detects potential security threats** (prompt injection, secret leak, malicious patch)
- **Fails to produce results** (agent failure, parse error)

When `continue-on-error: true` (the default), these problems produce warnings and safe outputs still proceed. When `continue-on-error: false`, they block safe outputs entirely.

</details>

<summary>How This Helps</summary>

This issue helps you:
- Track workflows where threat detection raised concerns
- Review patterns of detection warnings or failures
- Identify false positives or recurring issues with threat detection
- Monitor the health of the threat detection system

- The canonical JSON that was fed to SHA-256

title: [Feature] Add line breaks to error_summary in failures.json
description:
### Affected area

CLI (`vip` commands)

### What problem are you trying to solve?

The error_summary field does not have any line breaks. This makes it hard to visually parse and read the error. In comparison the feature key does have line breaks.

```bash
# Easy to read
cat report/failures.json | jq -r '.failures[0].feature' | bat
─────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
     │ STDIN
─────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   1 │ As a Posit Team administrator
   2 │ I want to verify that content can be deployed and executed
   3 │ So that I know the Connect publishing pipeline is functional
─────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

```bash
# hard to read
❯ cat report/failures.json | jq -r '.failures[0].error_summary' | bat --no-pager
─────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
     │ STDIN
─────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   1 │ test_deploy_plumber: an unexpected error occurred: Failed: Deployment failed: An error occurred while building
     │  your content. (Error code: r-missing-system-library) --- Task output --- Building Plumber API... Bundle creat
     │ ed with R version 4.6.0 is compatible with environment Local with R version 4.6.0 from /opt/R/4.6.0/bin/R Bund
     │ le requested R version 4.6.
...
```

### Proposed solution

Add line breaks to error_summary. E.g. each new log item should be a new line.

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

title: [Feature] Cleaner install with uv tool install
description:
### Affected area

CLI (`vip` commands)

### What problem are you trying to solve?

Installation involved cloning the repo. It can be done more simply.

### Proposed solution

I suggest that we can simplify the install instructions to:

```bash
uv tool install git+https://github.com/posit-dev/vip
which vip
# ~/.local/bin/vip
```

The quick start could look like this:

```bash
uv tool install git+https://github.com/posit-dev/vip
vip install
vip verify --connect-url https://connect.example.com --interactive-auth
```

## Background

A Posit customer's UAT plan included a handful of small, distinct gaps that don't merit their own large issue but each represent real coverage holes. Bundling them so they can be triaged together; each can be split out if/when it's picked up.

## Gap 1: Workbench sign-out flow

`src/vip_tests/workbench/test_auth.feature` validates login and homepage display but never signs out. The customer's plan walks through the sign-out drop-down because forgetting to invalidate a session has security implications.

**Proposed addition:**
```gherkin
Scenario: User can sign out of Workbench
  Given the user is logged in to Workbench
  When the user opens the user menu and clicks Sign Out
  Then the user is returned to the login page
  And the previous session cookie no longer authenticates
```

## Gap 2: AI features default-off in VS Code and Positron

The customer needs to confirm that AI/Copilot features in VS Code and Positron are disabled by default for compliance reasons. VIP's `test_ide_extensions.feature` validates extensions are installed but never asserts feature toggles.

**Proposed addition:**
```gherkin
Scenario Outline: AI features are disabled by default in <ide>
  Given the user is logged in to Workbench
  When the user starts a new <ide> session
  Then no AI inline-suggestion provider is active
  And no Chat panel is registered
  And the session is cleaned up

  Examples:
    | ide      |
    | VS Code  |
    | Positron |
```

The "no AI provider active" check needs concrete signals — typically the absence of `github.copilot` and similar extension IDs, plus a settings inspection. New TOML field `[workbench.ai_features] enabled = false` to declare expected state.

## Gap 3: Runtime IDE extension install from a terminal

`test_ide_extensions.feature` checks that **pre-installed** extensions are present. It doesn't validate that a user can run e.g. `code-server --install-extension <id>` and have the extension load. This matters for OpenVSX-backed deployments where extensions are pulled at runtime.

**Proposed addition:**
```gherkin
Scenario Outline: User can install an IDE extension at runtime in <ide>
  Given the user is logged in to Workbench
  When the user starts a new <ide> session
  And the user installs a known extension via the IDE terminal
  Then the extension appears in the installed list
  And the session is cleaned up

  Examples:
    | ide      |
    | VS Code  |
    | Positron |
```

## Acceptance criteria

- Three independent PRs, one per gap. Each can land separately.
- Sign-out scenario adds to existing `test_auth.feature`. AI defaults and runtime extension install each get a new feature file under `src/vip_tests/workbench/`.
- AI-defaults and runtime-install both depend on the in-session execution primitive (separate issue) for terminal access.

## Notes

These three are deliberately scoped so each one is a 1-3 file change. Pick them up opportunistically; nothing here blocks the bigger session-exec work.

title: feat(workbench): publish to Connect from a Workbench session
description:
## Background

VIP's `src/vip_tests/connect/test_content_deploy.feature` deploys Quarto, Plumber, R Shiny, Dash, R Markdown, Jupyter, and FastAPI bundles to Connect via the Connect API. That's the right shape for verifying the **Connect** publishing pipeline, but it skips the user-facing path most customers actually exercise during UAT: opening a Workbench session, then publishing from inside it.

A Posit customer's UAT plan flagged two specific cases:

1. Deploy a Python Shiny app from a VS Code/Positron terminal using `rsconnect-python`.
2. Deploy a Python Shiny app from a Positron session using the **Posit Publisher** extension UI.

Both are general capabilities and both are off the current VIP path.

## What's missing

- No scenario submits a deployment from within a Workbench session.
- No scenario uses Posit Publisher's UI flow.
- The existing `test_content_deploy.feature` has no Python Shiny scenario at all (R Shiny is covered, Python Shiny is not).

## Proposed scenarios

```gherkin
@workbench @connect
Feature: Publishing from a Workbench session

  Scenario: User deploys a Python Shiny app from the terminal via rsconnect-python
    Given the user is logged in to Workbench
    And Connect is configured in vip.toml
    When the user starts a new Positron session
    And the user creates a uv venv and installs rsconnect-python
    And the user configures a Connect server in rsconnect-python
    And the user deploys a minimal Python Shiny bundle from the terminal
    Then the deployment succeeds and the app responds over HTTP
    And I clean up the deployed content
    And the session is cleaned up

  Scenario: User deploys a Python Shiny app from Positron via Posit Publisher
    Given the user is logged in to Workbench
    And Connect is configured in vip.toml
    When the user starts a new Positron session
    And the user opens a Python Shiny project
    And the user uses Posit Publisher to deploy to the configured Connect server
    Then the deployment succeeds and the app responds over HTTP
    And I clean up the deployed content
    And the session is cleaned up
```

## Acceptance criteria

- A small Python Shiny test bundle (`app.py` + `requirements.txt`) lives under `src/vip_tests/_bundles/` for reuse.
- The terminal scenario depends on the in-session execution primitive (separate issue).
- The Publisher scenario is Playwright-driven against the VS Code-based Posit Publisher extension; it depends on the IDE-extension-install primitive (separate misc-gaps issue) so the test can ensure the extension is present before driving it.
- Cleanup deletes the content item via `connect_client` regardless of which path created it.

## Notes

- Both scenarios prove the chain Workbench → user-facing tool → Connect, which the current Connect-only deploy tests don't exercise.

title: feat(workbench): cover Git operations from a Workbench session
description:
## Background

VIP currently exercises Git only in two narrow places: a Connect-side git-backed Quarto deployment scenario (`src/vip_tests/connect/test_content_deploy.feature`) and an implicit GitHub mention in package install docs. It never validates that a user inside a Workbench session can actually clone, branch, commit, and push.

A Posit customer's UAT plan calls this out for two interfaces (RStudio Git GUI, and a terminal in any IDE) and two providers (GitHub, self-hosted Gitea). The substance generalizes: every Posit Team customer using Git from sessions wants this validated.

## What's missing

No `src/vip_tests/workbench/test_git_*.feature` exists. There's also no config block describing the test repos VIP should clone / push to.

## Proposed scenarios

```gherkin
@workbench @if_applicable
Feature: Git operations from Workbench sessions

  Scenario Outline: User can clone, commit, and push from the <ide> terminal
    Given the user is logged in to Workbench
    And a Git test repository is configured in vip.toml
    When the user starts a new <ide> session
    And the user clones the test repository in the terminal
    And the user creates a branch, commits a change, and pushes it
    Then the push succeeds and the new branch is visible on the remote
    And the test branch is cleaned up
    And the session is cleaned up

    Examples:
      | ide      |
      | RStudio  |
      | VS Code  |
      | Positron |

  Scenario: User can use the RStudio Git pane to commit and push
    Given the user is logged in to Workbench
    And a Git test repository is configured in vip.toml
    When the user starts a new RStudio session
    And the user opens the cloned repo as a project
    And the user commits and pushes a change via the Git pane
    Then the push succeeds and the new branch is visible on the remote
    And the test branch is cleaned up
    And the session is cleaned up
```

## Acceptance criteria

- New TOML block `[workbench.git_test]` with `clone_url`, `auth_method` (`ssh` | `https-token`), and a token reference (`VIP_GIT_TOKEN` env var). Skip cleanly when the block is absent.
- Terminal scenarios use the in-session execution primitive (separate issue) and require nothing provider-specific — they work identically against GitHub, Gitea, GitLab, or any reachable Git remote.
- The RStudio Git pane scenario is Playwright-driven and lives in its own `test_git_gui.feature`.
- Cleanup deletes any branch VIP pushed.

## Notes

- VIP must not push to `main` / `master`. The branch name should include `vip-` and a timestamp, and cleanup removes it.
- SSH authentication is the harder case (key forwarding); start with HTTPS + token to keep the first PR small.

title: feat(workbench): assert idle session auto-suspend behavior
description:
## Background

VIP's `test_sessions.feature` covers explicit suspend/resume but says nothing about idle behavior. A Posit customer's UAT plan distinguishes two related checks:

1. An **idle** session must auto-suspend after the configured idle timeout (e.g. 120 minutes).
2. An **active** session must **not** be suspended during a long-running computation (i.e. activity correctly resets the idle clock).

Both are general Posit Team behaviors driven by `session-timeout-minutes` / `session-timeout-suspend` in `rsession.conf`, not deployment-specific.

## What's missing

No scenario in `src/vip_tests/workbench/` validates timeouts. There's also no `idle_timeout_minutes` field in the Workbench config dataclass.

## Proposed scenarios

```gherkin
@workbench @slow
Feature: Workbench session idle behavior

  Scenario: Idle session auto-suspends after the configured timeout
    Given the user is logged in to Workbench
    And the configured idle timeout is known
    When the user starts a new RStudio session
    And the session sits idle for longer than the configured timeout
    Then the session reaches Suspended state without user action
    And the session is cleaned up

  Scenario: Active session is not suspended while work is running
    Given the user is logged in to Workbench
    And the configured idle timeout is known
    When the user starts a new RStudio session
    And the user runs a long-running computation that exceeds the idle timeout
    Then the session remains in Active state throughout
    And the session is cleaned up
```

## Acceptance criteria

- New TOML field `[workbench] idle_timeout_minutes = N` (the value the deployment is configured for; VIP doesn't enforce it, it asserts against it).
- Tests are tagged `@slow` and skipped by default unless the deployment opts in (idle timeouts under 30 min run fine; longer values would slow CI).
- Reuses the existing session lifecycle helpers; the active-session scenario uses the in-session execution primitive (separate issue) to start a long-running computation.

## Notes

- Allow a small grace window (e.g. timeout + 60s) to account for real-world clock drift.
- These two scenarios paired together prevent a class of false positives where a too-aggressive timeout silently kills user work.

title: feat(workbench): add Kubernetes autoscaling and capacity probes
description:
## Background

`src/vip_tests/workbench/test_session_capacity.feature` confirms that N sessions per resource profile reach Active state, but it doesn't probe what happens at the autoscaler boundary or verify that profile-defined CPU/memory limits are actually enforced. A Posit customer running a Kubernetes-backed Workbench UAT plan flagged six distinct scenarios in this area, all generic to Posit Team on Kubernetes (Launcher + Kubernetes plugin).

## What's missing

The session-capacity test launches sessions and asserts they go Active — it does not:

1. Confirm a new node was added to the pool when capacity was previously exhausted.
2. Confirm scale-up does **not** occur once the cluster is at its configured upper bound.
3. Race two session launches at the autoscaling threshold and confirm exactly one new node is added.
4. Race two launches above the cluster cap and confirm exactly one session lands.
5. Confirm a session lands on the correct node pool given the resource profile (i.e. profile -> pool routing rules).
6. Confirm the CPU/memory limits surfaced in the New Session dialog match the user's assigned Kubernetes profile.

## Proposed scenarios

```gherkin
@workbench @kubernetes
Feature: Workbench session capacity on Kubernetes

  Scenario: Cluster scales up when below the configured limit
    Given the cluster is below its configured node-pool maximum
    When I launch enough sessions to exhaust current capacity
    Then a new node is added to the node pool
    And all launched sessions reach Active state
    And I clean up all launched sessions

  Scenario: Cluster does not scale beyond the configured limit
    Given the cluster is at its configured node-pool maximum
    When I attempt to launch additional sessions
    Then no new nodes are added to the pool
    And the over-cap sessions remain in Pending or are rejected
    And I clean up all launched sessions

  Scenario: Quick-succession launches at the autoscale threshold add only one node
    Given the cluster is one session away from triggering autoscale
    When I launch two sessions in quick succession
    Then exactly one new node is added to the node pool
    And I clean up all launched sessions

  Scenario: Quick-succession launches above the cluster cap admit only one session
    Given the cluster is at its configured node-pool maximum minus one
    When I launch two sessions in quick succession
    Then exactly one session reaches Active state
    And I clean up all launched sessions

  Scenario: Resource profile routes the session to the expected node pool
    Given a resource profile is configured for a specific node pool
    When the user launches a session with that profile
    Then the session pod is scheduled on the expected pool
    And the session is cleaned up

  Scenario: New Session dialog reflects the user's profile limits
    Given the user is logged in to Workbench
    When the user opens the New Session dialog
    Then the CPU and memory caps shown match the user's assigned profile
```

## Acceptance criteria

- New `test_session_capacity_k8s.feature` (or extend the existing capacity feature) with the six scenarios.
- New TOML config block under `[workbench.kubernetes]` for: node-pool name(s), expected per-profile pool mapping, expected per-profile CPU/memory caps, and the credentials VIP will use to query the cluster.
- A Kubernetes client wrapper under `src/vip/clients/kubernetes.py` that uses `kubectl` (already a VIP install dependency on cluster admin runs) or the `kubernetes` Python SDK. Read-only access — VIP must not mutate cluster state.
- Skip cleanly when no Kubernetes config block is provided so non-K8s deployments are unaffected.

## Notes

- The "quick succession" scenarios likely need a thread or asyncio gather of two launches; sequential Playwright will not exercise the race.
- VIP already supports cluster-aware modes via `src/vip/cluster/` — that infrastructure can supply the kubeconfig.

title: feat(workbench): verify expected R/Python versions on the Workbench side
description:
## Background

VIP already verifies that the expected R, Python, and Quarto versions are registered with **Connect** (`src/vip_tests/connect/test_runtime_versions.feature`, driven by `expected_r_versions` / `expected_python_versions` in `vip.toml`). It does **not** verify the same on the **Workbench** side, where versions are surfaced through a different mechanism (loaded from `r-versions` / `python-versions` config and exposed in the New Session dialog and in-session interpreter pickers).

A Posit customer running UAT flagged this as a gap — they need to confirm that the runtimes their users will actually pick from in Workbench match the agreed list, with EOL versions excluded. This is general Posit Team content, not deployment-specific.

## What's missing

There is no `src/vip_tests/workbench/test_runtime_versions.feature`. `expected_r_versions` and `expected_python_versions` from `vip.toml` are read by the Connect tests only.

## Proposed scenarios

```gherkin
@workbench
Feature: Workbench R and Python versions
  Scenario: Expected R versions are available in Workbench
    Given the user is logged in to Workbench
    And expected R versions are specified in vip.toml
    When the user opens the New Session dialog for RStudio
    Then all expected R versions are present in the version selector
    And no unexpected R versions are offered

  Scenario: Expected Python versions are available in Workbench
    Given the user is logged in to Workbench
    And expected Python versions are specified in vip.toml
    When the user opens the New Session dialog for JupyterLab
    Then all expected Python versions are present in the kernel selector
    And no unexpected Python versions are offered

  Scenario: An RStudio project opens with the expected R version
    Given the user is logged in to Workbench
    When the user starts a new RStudio session pinned to a specific R version
    Then the session reports that R version via R.version.string
    And the session is cleaned up
```

## Acceptance criteria

- New `test_runtime_versions.feature` + `test_runtime_versions.py` under `src/vip_tests/workbench/`.
- Reuses the existing `expected_r_versions` / `expected_python_versions` config fields — no new TOML keys.
- Optional `unexpected_r_versions: bool` flag (default true) controls whether the "no unexpected versions" assertion is strict; some customers want the assertion to be allow-list, others additive.
- The third scenario depends on the in-session execution primitive (separate issue) for the `R.version.string` read.

title: feat(workbench): cover Workbench Jobs and Background Jobs
description:
## Background

A Posit customer mapped their UAT test plan against VIP and identified Workbench Jobs as a feature with no coverage today. Both **Workbench Jobs** (run on a separate Kubernetes pod) and **Background Jobs** (run in the same session) are first-class Workbench features that customers exercise during acceptance — there's nothing deployment-specific about them.

## What's missing

`src/vip_tests/workbench/` has no `test_jobs.feature`. The existing tests cover session launch, suspend/resume, and capacity, but never submit a script as a job.

## Proposed scenarios

```gherkin
@workbench
Feature: Workbench Jobs and Background Jobs

  Scenario: User can submit a Workbench Job from RStudio Pro
    Given the user is logged in to Workbench
    When the user starts a new RStudio session
    And the user submits a short R script as a Workbench Job
    Then the job reaches Completed state
    And the job log contains the expected output
    And the session is cleaned up

  Scenario: User can submit a Background Job from RStudio Pro
    Given the user is logged in to Workbench
    When the user starts a new RStudio session
    And the user submits a short R script as a Background Job
    Then the Background Jobs pane shows the job as Completed
    And the session is cleaned up
```

## Acceptance criteria

- A new `src/vip_tests/workbench/test_jobs.feature` with both scenarios, tagged `@workbench`.
- Step definitions in `src/vip_tests/workbench/test_jobs.py` that drive the RStudio Workbench Jobs / Background Jobs UI via Playwright.
- A short bundled test R script (e.g. `Sys.sleep(2); cat("hello from job\n")`) shipped with the test, written into the session's working directory.
- Cleanup: any leftover job artifacts removed.

## Notes

- Workbench Jobs use Launcher infrastructure, so this scenario also indirectly verifies the Launcher is functional — a useful side effect.
- This depends on the in-session execution primitive (separate issue) only for writing the script file into the session; otherwise it's standalone.

title: feat(workbench): add an in-session execution primitive
description:
## Background

A Posit customer running a UAT process for their Posit Team deployment maintains a private test plan covering ~47 acceptance scenarios. When their test plan was mapped to VIP's current coverage, the largest single gap was clear: VIP validates *that* a Workbench session launches and *that* repos.conf points at the right URL, but it never executes anything inside the session beyond `1 + 1` in the RStudio console (`src/vip_tests/workbench/test_ide_launch.py:312`).

That gap blocks ~15 distinct customer-facing checks. Rather than file each one, this issue proposes an in-session execution primitive that the others can be built on.

## What's missing

VIP has page objects for RStudio, VS Code, JupyterLab, and Positron (`src/vip_tests/workbench/pages/`) and reliable session launch + cleanup. What it doesn't have is a reusable way to:

- Run an R expression in an RStudio console and assert on the captured output (`1 + 1` -> `[1] 2` is the only example today, hard-coded in `rstudio_executes_r_code`).
- Run a Python expression in a Positron / JupyterLab / VS Code session.
- Run a shell command in an IDE terminal and read its output.
- Render a document (`rmarkdown::render`, `quarto render`) from inside a session and verify the artifact lands on disk.

## Acceptance criteria

A test author should be able to write a step like:

```python
result = rstudio_eval(page, "packageVersion('Matrix')")
assert "1." in result
```

...and have a single helper handle console focus, typing, Enter, output capture, and timeouts. Equivalent helpers should exist for Python (Positron console, JupyterLab cell, VS Code Python extension) and IDE terminals.

## Issues this unblocks

These are the customer scenarios that currently can't be expressed in VIP because the primitive is missing. None are deployment-specific; every Posit Team customer running UAT would care:

- Install an R package from PPM and verify it loaded as a binary
- Install an R package from GitHub via `remotes::install_github`
- Restore an `renv` project (`renv::restore()`)
- Install a geospatial package (`sf`) and confirm GDAL/PROJ/GEOS are reachable
- Knit RMarkdown to PDF / Word / HTML
- Knit RMarkdown using `flextable`
- Render a Python Quarto file
- Create a `uv` virtual environment from a VS Code/Positron terminal
- Query a database from R via DBI / odbc
- Query a database from Python via SQLAlchemy / psycopg
- Use `keyring` to retrieve a stored credential
- Run an R Shiny app (`shiny::runApp`) inside RStudio and confirm it serves
- Detect which R/Python versions are available *inside* a Workbench session (the Connect-side check at `src/vip_tests/connect/test_runtime_versions.feature` doesn't tell you what users see in Workbench)

## Suggested shape

- New module `src/vip_tests/workbench/exec.py` housing `rstudio_eval`, `positron_eval`, `terminal_run`, etc.
- Each helper takes `page: Page` and an expression string, returns captured stdout/stderr or raises on timeout.
- Step definitions for new scenarios (RMarkdown knit, package install, etc.) live in their own `test_*.py` files and call into `exec.py`.
- A Workbench config field for "test packages to install" so the package-install scenarios are deployment-agnostic.

title: [Feature] add example of adding a custom test extension
description:
### Affected area

Cross-product tests

### What problem are you trying to solve?

Customers need to extend VIP with specific requirements for a given installation. Consider a GxP deployment which needs to verify specific versions of R and Python are available and specific package versions are able to install on both workbench and connect.

### Proposed solution

VIP already has support for loading tests from an external directory, but I would like to see a complete example showing how to create a vip test extension. Perhaps a vip subcommand for adding an example test case. The test case should verify that both R and Python versions are available in both Workbench and Connect, and should verify that a python and R package are installable. Perhaps using the DESeq2 and PyDeSEQ2 packages.

### Alternatives considered

An alternative to a subcommand for adding a test extension would be doing a documentation only example, but that requires a lot more copy and paste for the end user. I prefer having a fully functioning helper for adding a test so an end user can immediately see the new test running and iterate on revising the test definition.

title: docs: plan for #288 — improved timeout configuration
description:
This PR proposes a plan for implementing comprehensive timeout configuration in VIP (#288).

## Plan Summary

The plan introduces a centralized `TimeoutConfig` dataclass in `src/vip/config.py` that replaces hardcoded timeout values across the test suite. This enables users testing on resource-constrained infrastructure to scale timeouts up or down via `vip.toml` without forking the codebase.

**Key changes:**
- New `[timeouts]` section in config with ~15 semantic timeout fields
- Replace hardcoded constants in `src/vip_tests/workbench/conftest.py`
- Thread timeout config through httpx clients and Playwright browser tests
- Add selftests for config parsing

**Merging this PR will trigger an implementation PR** — comment to iterate on the plan first.

Closes \#288

title: feat: improved timeout configuration
description: Timeouts were a struggle for testing Marketplaces instances with VIP. We typically use smaller VMs for QA testing which translates to extended load times for operations like launching sessions in Workbench or deploying content in Connect. Some timeouts are configurable for VIP, but not many. We should consider either significantly extending the default timeouts or adding more configuration levers to scale timeouts up or down as needed.

title: fix(manifest): treat empty .vip-install.json as missing (closes #283)
description:
Closes \#283

Fixed a UX issue where an empty `.vip-install.json` file (zero bytes or whitespace-only) would error out with `ManifestError: corrupt JSON` instead of being treated like a missing file. The fix adds a check in `manifest.load()` to return `None` when the file content is empty or whitespace-only, matching the behavior for missing files.

## Changes

- Modified `src/vip/install/manifest.py::load()` to strip and check for empty content before attempting JSON parsing
- Added `test_load_empty_file_returns_none()` in `selftests/install/test_manifest.py` that verifies both empty and whitespace-only files return `None`

## Demo

### Test

The new selftest verifies that both empty files and whitespace-only files are handled gracefully:

```python
def test_load_empty_file_returns_none(tmp_path: Path):
    """Empty or whitespace-only manifest files are treated as missing."""
    path = tmp_path / ".vip-install.json"
    path.write_text("")
    assert load(path) is None
    path.write_text("   \n\t  ")
    assert load(path) is None
```

title: vip install errors on empty .vip-install.json instead of treating it as fresh
description:
## What I observed

When `.vip-install.json` exists but is empty (e.g., truncated to zero bytes by a previous interrupted write, or accidentally created with `touch`), `vip install` errors out with a confusing message and refuses to proceed.

## Reproduction

```
echo -n "" > .vip-install.json
uv run vip install --skip-system
```

## Expected

Empty (or whitespace-only) manifest files should be treated the same as missing files — `manifest.load()` returns `None` and we proceed with a fresh install.

## Actual

```
ManifestError: Manifest at .vip-install.json is corrupt JSON (Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)). Delete it manually to retry.
```

Telling the user to delete the file works but it's not great UX — a zero-byte manifest is unambiguous, we don't need user intervention.

## Suggested fix

In `src/vip/install/manifest.py::load`, check whether `path.read_text().strip()` is empty before passing to `json.loads`, and return `None` if so. Selftest: add a case in `selftests/install/` (or wherever the existing manifest tests live) that writes an empty file and asserts `load()` returns `None`.

title: fix(workbench): failed tests leave orphaned sessions that aren't cleaned up
description:
## Problem

When VIP tests fail mid-execution (e.g., during IDE interaction), the sessions they launched are not reliably cleaned up. Users must manually quit orphaned sessions after a failed VIP run.

**Observed at:** PHS UAT on 2026-05-20 — multiple orphaned sessions visible on the Workbench homepage after test failures.

**From transcript:**
> "if it fails on any of its tests, it doesn't clean up the old sessions, so you'll have to come out here and quit some of these"

## Current Behavior

The `session_context` fixture has best-effort cleanup, and `_cleanup_sessions` autouse fixture exists. However, sessions that fail during IDE interaction (after join but before cleanup step) may not be properly terminated, especially if:
- The Playwright page is in an unexpected state (inside a session, not on `/home`)
- Navigation to `/home` fails
- The session checkbox/quit interaction fails

## Expected Behavior

All sessions created by VIP should be cleaned up regardless of test outcome. Options:
1. Use the Workbench API (`DELETE /api/sessions/{id}`) for cleanup instead of UI interaction — more reliable
2. Add a session-scoped finalizer that queries the API for sessions matching the VIP naming pattern (`VIP *`) and force-quits them
3. Add a `vip cleanup` CLI command that removes any VIP-created sessions

## Suggested Fix

API-based cleanup is the most robust:
```python
# In fixture finalizer or conftest cleanup
sessions = workbench_client.list_sessions()
for s in sessions:
    if s["label"].startswith("VIP "):
        workbench_client.quit_session(s["id"])
```

This avoids depending on Playwright page state for cleanup.

title: fix(workbench): test ordering — extension tests should depend on IDE launch tests
description:
## Problem

IDE extension tests (`test_ide_extensions.py`) run **before** IDE launch tests (`test_ide_launch.py`) due to alphabetical ordering. This means:

1. Extension tests launch sessions independently to check for extensions
2. Launch tests then launch sessions again to verify basic IDE functionality

This is logically backwards — if an IDE can't launch, there's no point checking its extensions. Additionally, extension tests that fail due to launch issues produce confusing error output rather than clean skip messages.

**Observed at:** PHS UAT on 2026-05-20 — `test_positron_extensions` failed with a 90s timeout while `test_launch_positron` was SKIPPED (Positron not configured). The extension test wasted time launching Positron when the launch test already knew it shouldn't run.

## Expected Behavior

Extension tests should:
1. Only run if the corresponding IDE launch test passed, OR
2. Be ordered after launch tests so that failures cascade logically, OR  
3. Share the "is this IDE available?" gate with launch tests

## Additional Context (from transcript)

> "if what this test is doing is launching a session and checking to make sure the extensions load... then we should do that **after** we've tested to make sure sessions actually launch"

> "the ordering of the individual tests... it looks like it's alphabetical now, but we need to think about the logical order to run the test from"

## Suggested Fix

Options:
1. **pytest ordering plugin** — use `pytest-ordering` or custom marks to enforce launch→extensions order
2. **Dependency marks** — add a custom `@pytest.mark.depends_on("test_launch_vscode")` pattern
3. **Shared skip logic** — extension tests check if the IDE is configured/launchable before attempting session creation (partially exists but inconsistent for Positron)

title: fix(workbench): RStudio launch test fails when .Rprofile has interactive prompt
description:
## Problem

`test_launch_rstudio[chromium]` fails because the customer has an Acceptable Usage Policy (AUP) prompt in their `.Rprofile` that blocks the R console before VIP can execute `1 + 1`.

**Observed at:** PHS UAT (pwb-uat.publichealthscotland.org) on 2026-05-20

**Error output:**
```
Locator expected to contain text '[1] 2'
Actual value: ... Please type 'agree' at the prompt to confirm you are an authorised
user, and you have read and understood the Acceptable Usage Policy: Type ok: 1 + 1 Type ok:
```

The test typed `1 + 1` and pressed Enter, but R was waiting for the user to type `agree` or `ok` at the AUP prompt first. The expression `1 + 1` was consumed by the `readline()` in the `.Rprofile` script and treated as invalid AUP acceptance input.

## Expected Behavior

VIP should either:
1. Detect that the console is showing a non-standard prompt and handle it, or
2. Document this as a known limitation and skip gracefully with a descriptive message, or
3. Wait longer / look for the standard R prompt (`>`) before sending code

## Suggested Fix

Before typing `1 + 1`, the test should wait for the R prompt character (`>`) to appear in the console output, indicating R is ready to accept expressions. If the prompt doesn't appear within the timeout, fail with a message indicating that a startup script may be blocking the console.

Alternatively, consider:
- Launching RStudio with `--no-restore` or equivalent to skip `.Rprofile`
- Detecting common AUP patterns and typing the acceptance keyword

## Context

This is a common pattern in healthcare/government orgs where shared compute resources require users to acknowledge usage policies before each session. The `.Rprofile` uses `readline()` to gate access.

## Reproduction

Run VIP against any Workbench instance where users have a `.Rprofile` that prompts for interactive input before giving the R console prompt.

title: fix(workbench): positron extensions test looks for wrong element selector
description:
## Problem

`test_positron_extensions[chromium]` fails looking for `get_by_role("button", name="home Posit Workbench")` but the actual Positron UI has a **tab** element named "Posit Workbench" instead.

**Observed at:** PHS UAT (pwb-uat.publichealthscotland.org) on 2026-05-20

**Error output:**
```
Locator expected to be visible
waiting for get_by_role("button", name="home Posit Workbench")
```

The accessibility tree dump shows Positron loaded successfully with a tab labeled "Posit Workbench" visible in the sidebar:
```
- tab "Posit Workbench"
```

The step "the Posit Workbench extension is visible in Positron" (`test_ide_extensions.py:280-287`) waits for a **button** with name "home Posit Workbench", but newer Positron versions appear to render this as a tab in the Activity Bar rather than a button.

## Expected Behavior

The selector should match the actual UI element that represents the Posit Workbench extension presence — whether it's rendered as a button or a tab.

## Suggested Fix

Update the selector to look for the Posit Workbench extension indicator using a more resilient locator, e.g.:
- `page.get_by_role("tab", name="Posit Workbench")` or
- A locator that accepts either role

## Reproduction

Run VIP against a Workbench instance with a recent Positron version installed.

title: fix(workbench): login test checks username but new homepage shows display name
description:
## Problem

`test_workbench_login[chromium]` asserts that `#current-user` text equals `test_username` (the login ID). On the new Workbench homepage, `#current-user` displays the user's **full display name** instead.

**Observed at:** PHS UAT (pwb-uat.publichealthscotland.org) on 2026-05-20

**Error output:**
```
Locator expected to have text 'shaneh02'
Actual value: Shane Halloran
```

The test step "the current user is shown in the header" (`test_auth.py:69-73`) does:
```python
expect(page.locator(Homepage.CURRENT_USER)).to_have_text(test_username)
```

## Expected Behavior

The test should accept either the login username OR the display name as valid, since Workbench shows the display name on the new homepage UI.

## Suggested Fix

Either:
1. Change assertion to `to_contain_text` matching a substring, or
2. Accept both username and display name (query the API for the user's display name and accept either), or
3. Verify the element exists and is non-empty rather than asserting exact text match against the login username

Option 3 is the most resilient since we've already verified login succeeded by reaching the homepage.

## Reproduction

Run VIP against any Workbench instance where the LDAP/IdP display name differs from the login username (very common).

title: fix(auth): interactive auth fails to mint Connect API key
description:
## Problem

`_create_api_key_via_session()` in `src/vip/auth.py:950` fails to mint a Connect API key after interactive OIDC/SAML authentication completes. The function uses session cookies extracted from the Playwright browser context to call `/__api__/v1/user`, but the request returns a non-success status (likely 401 Unauthorized), causing VIP to fall back to requiring a manually-created `VIP_CONNECT_API_KEY`.

This failure occurred on both Connect 2023.x and Connect 2026.x instances, confirming it is not version-specific. The interactive login itself succeeds (user is authenticated in the browser), but the subsequent API call using extracted cookies fails.

## Observed During

VIP verification call with Intuitive Surgical (2026-05-14). Environment: AWS EKS, SAML auth via Okta, AWS ALB in front of Connect.

Workaround used: Customer manually created API keys via the Connect UI and exported `VIP_CONNECT_API_KEY`.

## Suspected Causes

1. **XSRF token extraction failure** — `_xsrf_from_page()` may not find the XSRF cookie under the expected names (`RSC-XSRF` or `RSC-XSRF-legacy`) in an Okta/SAML flow
2. **Cookie path scoping** — The ALB may set cookies with a path that doesn't match what Playwright returns from `page.context.cookies(me_url)`
3. **SameSite/Secure cookie attributes** — The cookie may not transfer correctly when extracted from a headed browser and replayed via httpx
4. **SAML-specific session handling** — SAML sessions may use different cookie names or session mechanisms than OIDC

## Diagnostic Info Available

The function already prints diagnostics on failure:
```
>>> Warning: GET /v1/user returned HTTP {status}: {body_snippet}
>>> Mint diagnostic: X-Rsc-Xsrf header was {preview}
```

We need verbose output from a reproduction to see these messages.

## Relevant Code

- `src/vip/auth.py:950-1029` — `_create_api_key_via_session()`
- `src/vip/auth.py:998` — `_xsrf_from_page()` call
- `src/vip/auth.py:1006-1010` — cookie extraction from browser context
- `src/vip/plugin.py:216` — warning message when minting fails

## Reproduction

- Deploy Connect behind an AWS ALB with SAML (Okta) auth
- Run `vip verify --connect-url <url> --interactive-auth`
- Complete login in the browser window
- Observe that API key minting fails (warning printed, tests fall back to manual key)

## Next Steps

- Get verbose output from the customer (Kamal offered to email the trace)
- Reproduce against an internal SAML-configured Connect instance
- Check if the issue is specific to SAML vs OIDC, or if it affects all IdP flows behind an ALB

title: fix(ssl): HTTPS redirect test fails behind AWS ALB
description:
## Problem

The "HTTP redirects to HTTPS" test in `src/vip_tests/cross_product/test_ssl.py:102-111` asserts that an HTTP request returns status 301, 302, 307, or 308 with a `Location` header starting with `https://`. When the product sits behind an AWS ALB, the redirect behavior differs from what the test expects, causing a false failure even though the redirect works correctly (confirmed manually in a browser).

Possible ALB behaviors that would fail this assertion:
- ALB returns a 200 after internally upgrading to HTTPS (listener rule does the redirect before the request reaches the product)
- ALB uses a non-standard redirect mechanism
- The HTTP port is handled differently at the ALB layer (e.g., connection upgrade rather than redirect response)

## Observed During

VIP verification call with Intuitive Surgical (2026-05-14). Both Connect and Workbench sit behind separate AWS ALBs on EKS. Manually navigating to the HTTP URL in a browser redirects to HTTPS correctly, but the VIP test reported failure on both products (2023 and 2026 instances).

## Expected Behavior

The test should handle common load balancer redirect patterns:
1. Standard 3xx redirect with HTTPS `Location` header (current check) 
2. ALB-style behavior where HTTP port may not respond directly (already handled via `port_closed` path)
3. Follow one redirect and verify the final URL is HTTPS (e.g., `follow_redirects=True` then assert `resp.url.scheme == "https"`)

Option 3 is probably the most robust — it tests the actual user experience (does HTTP end up at HTTPS?) rather than the specific mechanism.

## Relevant Code

- `src/vip_tests/cross_product/test_ssl.py:77-111` — `request_http()` step + `redirects_to_https()` assertion
- `src/vip_tests/cross_product/test_ssl.feature:19-22` — the scenario outline

## Investigation Needed

Reproduce with a product behind an AWS ALB to determine exactly what HTTP response code/behavior the ALB returns when `follow_redirects=False`. This will clarify whether we need to:
- Add more accepted status codes
- Follow redirects and check the final scheme
- Handle the case where the ALB transparently upgrades without a client-visible redirect

title: fix(connect): test_list_users fails when no test user is configured
description:
## Problem

The "Users can be listed" scenario in `src/vip_tests/connect/test_users.feature` unconditionally asserts that the test user exists in the user list (line 17: `And the test user exists in the user list`). When no `VIP_TEST_USERNAME` is configured (common for interactive auth flows where the user authenticates directly), the `test_username` fixture yields an empty string, and the step at `src/vip_tests/connect/test_users.py:51-55` searches for `""` in the username list and fails.

## Observed During

VIP verification call with Intuitive Surgical (2026-05-14). They used `--interactive-auth` without setting `VIP_TEST_USERNAME`. The user list endpoint returned successfully and showed real users, but the test failed because it tried to find empty-string in the list.

## Expected Behavior

When no test user is explicitly configured, the `the test user exists in the user list` step should either:
1. Skip gracefully (`pytest.skip("No test user configured — skipping user lookup assertion")`)
2. Substitute the currently authenticated user (from the `/v1/user` endpoint) as the test user to verify

Option 1 is simpler and still validates the important part (the endpoint works and returns users). The "user list is not empty" step already confirms the API is functional.

## Relevant Code

- `src/vip_tests/connect/test_users.feature:17` — the step that triggers the failure
- `src/vip_tests/connect/test_users.py:51-55` — `check_test_user_in_list()` splits on `@` and asserts membership
- `src/vip_tests/conftest.py` — `test_username` fixture (yields empty string when not set)

title: fix(workbench): session launch tests fail with SAML/Okta auth — login not shared from interactive auth
description:
## Context

During a VIP verification call with Intuitive Surgical (2026-05-14), all Workbench IDE session launch tests (`test_launch_rstudio`, `test_launch_vscode`, `test_launch_jupyter`) failed with "login failed" errors on **both** their Workbench 2023 and Workbench 2026 instances.

Their environment:
- AWS EKS deployment
- SAML authentication via Okta
- ALB in front of each product (separate ALBs for Connect and Workbench)
- Interactive auth (`--interactive-auth`) was used

Connect tests passed (content publishing worked for all types), but the interactive auth session captured during Connect login did not carry over to Workbench.

## Root Cause (Suspected)

`workbench_login()` in `src/vip_tests/workbench/conftest.py:110` skips when `auth_provider != "password"` and there's no pre-loaded session. When `--interactive-auth` IS used, the storage state is captured from the Connect auth flow, but the SAML session cookie is scoped to the Connect hostname — it doesn't authenticate Workbench on a separate ALB/hostname.

The code at line 126-129 explicitly handles this case:
```python
pytest.skip(
    "Interactive auth storage state did not authenticate Workbench. "
    "The OIDC session may not be shared between Connect and Workbench."
)
```

But the test reports "login failed" rather than gracefully handling the separate auth domain.

## What the Customer Saw

```
FAILED test_launch_rstudio - login failed
FAILED test_launch_vscode - login failed  
FAILED test_launch_jupyter - login failed
```

With `--verbose`, no additional actionable trace was produced beyond the login failure.

## Expected Behavior

When interactive auth is used and the products are on separate auth domains (common with ALB + SAML setups), VIP should either:
1. Prompt for a separate Workbench interactive auth session, or
2. Attempt to use the same IdP session cookies (if the IdP domain is shared even when product domains differ), or
3. Provide a clear skip message explaining that Workbench requires its own auth session

## Reproduction

- Deploy Workbench behind a separate ALB from Connect
- Configure SAML (Okta) auth  
- Run `vip verify --workbench-url <url> --interactive-auth`
- Observe that the interactive auth captured for Connect does not authenticate Workbench

## Additional Context

- Gong call recording: https://us-1237.app.gong.io/call?id=348267831445141666
- Customer offered to email full verbose trace stack output
- Sam suspects the specific issue is SAML vs OIDC handling — VIP may be "looking for the wrong thing when it comes to logging in" for SAML providers
- The 2023 Workbench failures were initially attributed to UI version differences, but the same failure occurred on 2026, confirming it's an auth issue not a selector issue
