title: [Bug] Two vacuous assertions in cross_product/test_ssl.py, exposed once the file started running
description:
Child of #409. Found while making `cross_product/test_ssl.py` actually execute for #546 — until now every scenario in that file skipped, so these two problems were invisible.

**1. `the HTTP port is not open` asserts nothing.** `src/vip_tests/cross_product/test_ssl.py:148`:

```python
@then("the HTTP port is not open")
def http_port_closed(http_response):
    # This step is an alternative - if HTTP redirected, that's fine too.
    pass
```

The feature file states it as a requirement:

```gherkin
Scenario Outline: HTTP redirects to HTTPS for <product>
  ...
  Then the response redirects to HTTPS
  And the HTTP port is not open
```

A reader of the `.feature` file reasonably concludes VIP verifies the plain-HTTP port is closed. It does not. The preceding step already accepts a redirect, so this one has nothing left to check — but then it should not be in the feature file, or it should assert the narrower thing it means (for example: if the HTTP port answers, the only acceptable response is a redirect to the HTTPS URL, never content).

**2. "not expired" computes no expiry.** `test_ssl.py:62`:

```python
@then("the certificate is valid and not expired")
def cert_valid(cert_info):
    assert cert_info["error"] is None, ...
    assert cert_info["cert"] is not None, ...
```

An already-expired certificate does fail, because `ssl.create_default_context()` rejects it during the handshake, so the scenario is not wrong. But the step name promises a date check that does not exist, and the genuinely useful version of this — warning that a certificate expires within N days, before an outage happens — is absent. `getpeercert()` already returns `notAfter`, so the data is in hand.

## Why this matters more than it looks

These are the residue of a file that never ran. #551 covers the sibling problem (tests that gate a required check while always skipping). This is the other failure mode: a step that runs, passes, and verifies nothing.

An audit of every `given`/`when`/`then` in `src/vip_tests` for a body of only `pass` found exactly two hits — this one, and `prerequisites/test_expected_failure.py:31`, which is a legitimately empty `given`. So the suite is broadly honest; this is a contained fix rather than a pattern.

## Acceptance

- `the HTTP port is not open` either asserts something real or leaves the feature file.
- The expiry step either computes an expiry margin or is renamed to describe what it actually checks.
- Ideally an expiry-margin assertion with a configurable threshold, since certificate expiry is a genuine cause of production outages and is exactly what a verification suite should catch early.

title: fix(report): `vip report` fails unless report extra installed AND Quarto kernel is pinned
description:
## Summary

`vip report` fails out of the box after `uv tool install posit-vip` for **two independent reasons**. Both must be fixed for the command to work standalone.

## Reproduction

```bash
uv tool install posit-vip        # NO [report] extra
cd ~/some-project                 # any dir with its own .venv
uv run vip report                 # or plain: vip report
```

Two distinct failures, in sequence:

### 1. `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'vip.gherkin'` / `No module named 'nbformat'`

`vip report` shells out to `quarto render`, which spins up **its own Jupyter kernel** to execute the Python cells in `report/details.qmd` and `report/index.qmd`. Those cells `import vip.gherkin` / `vip.reporting`, so the kernel's interpreter needs **both**:

- `posit-vip` itself (for `vip.gherkin`, `vip.reporting`), and
- the report/Jupyter stack (`nbformat`, `nbclient`, `jupyter`, …), currently only in the **optional** `[report]` extra.

A bare `uv tool install posit-vip` installs neither Jupyter (extra not requested) into an environment Quarto can see. Users have to know to run `uv tool install --force 'posit-vip[report]'` — undiscoverable.

### 2. Quarto picks the wrong Python interpreter

Even with `[report]` installed into the tool venv, Quarto does **not** use it. Quarto's kernel-discovery honours the ambient `VIRTUAL_ENV` (set by `uv run`, or an activated venv) and otherwise falls back to `/usr/bin/python3`. So:

- `uv run vip report` from another project → Quarto uses **that project's** venv (no `posit-vip`) → `ModuleNotFoundError: vip.gherkin`.
- plain `vip report` with nothing activated → Quarto uses `/usr/bin/python3` → `ModuleNotFoundError: nbformat`.

The interpreter that actually has everything — the one running `vip` itself (`sys.executable`) — is never the one Quarto chooses.

### Confirmed workaround (proves the fix)

```bash
uv tool install --force 'posit-vip[report]'
QUARTO_PYTHON="$(uv tool dir)/posit-vip/bin/python" vip report --open   # renders cleanly
```

## Fix

1. **Fold the report deps into base `[project.dependencies]`** so any `posit-vip` install (including bare `uv tool install posit-vip`) can render. Keep `[report]` as a back-compat alias so `posit-vip[report]` still resolves.
2. **`vip report` sets `QUARTO_PYTHON=sys.executable`** when it shells out, pinning Quarto's kernel to the same interpreter running `vip` — which, after (1), always has the full stack. This also neutralises the `uv run` / `VIRTUAL_ENV` hijack.

## Env observed

- `posit-vip 0.58.8`, Quarto 1.8.27, uv 0.11.28, WSL2.

title: [Bug] Connect smoke gate can fail on transient rspm-sync.rstudio.com resets during packrat restore
description:
Child of #409.

`Connect Smoke Tests Status` is a required check, and it can go red for reasons entirely outside this repository.

Observed on a dispatch run of `connect-smoke.yml` (run `30398775778`), on the `2026.06.0` leg only:

```
Installing xtable (1.8-8) ...
curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: Connection reset by peer in connection to rspm-sync.rstudio.com:443
curl: HTTP 307 https://rspm-sync.rstudio.com/bin/4.5-jammy/2b93...tar.gz
Error in download.file(url, destfile, method, mode = "wb", ...) : 'curl' call had nonzero exit status
...
Error in getSourceForPkgRecord(...) : Failed to download current version of fontawesome(0.5.3)
Unable to fully restore the R packages associated with this deployment.
```

`test_deploy_plumber` and `test_deploy_shiny` both failed. The same two tests passed on the `release` and `2026.05.1` legs of the same run, so this is transient upstream behaviour, not a version-specific bug.

## Why it happens

Connect resolves R packages over the public internet on every run. The deploy log shows the repository set Connect hands to packrat:

```
- CRAN  = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/jammy/latest"
- RSPM  = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/jammy/latest"
- CRAN.1 = "https://p3m.dev/cran/latest"
```

with binaries served from `rspm-sync.rstudio.com`. Any reset, 307 loop or slow response there fails a deploy and therefore a required check. Note the retry behaviour is inconsistent: some packages recovered on a second attempt within the same run (`curl`, `Rcpp`, `xtable`) while others gave up after two (`otel`, `fontawesome`).

## Options

1. **Retry the deploy at the test level.** Cheapest, and honest — deploys are genuinely flaky against a live CDN. Risks masking a real regression in deployment if the retry is too generous.
2. **Reduce the package surface.** The bundles pull a full transitive closure (`fontawesome`, `xtable`, `otel`, …). A minimal Shiny app with fewer dependencies would have fewer chances to fail. Trades realism for reliability.
3. **Pin to a dated PPM snapshot** rather than `latest`, so the URL set is stable and more likely to be cached. Does not fix a connection reset.
4. **Accept and re-run.** Current de facto behaviour, which means a required check that is sometimes wrong.
5. **Pre-warm the packrat cache** in the container before the deploy tests run, so a single transient failure does not fail the suite.

## Acceptance

- A transient upstream CDN failure does not fail the `Connect Smoke Tests Status` required check.
- Whatever mitigation is chosen does not hide a genuine deployment regression — a deploy that fails for a reason other than package download must still fail the suite.

## Context

Found while verifying #552 (the gate/nightly tier split for the cross-product suite). Worth noting the wider point that surfaced there: the Connect gate is not hermetic and cannot easily be made so, because installing R packages is exactly what the deploy tests are meant to exercise.

title: [Bug] test_packages sits on the Workbench gate but always skips after 29s of work
description:
Child of #409. Found while measuring the Workbench suite for #539.

`workbench/test_packages.py` is in the PR-gated set of `workbench-smoke.yml` and skips on every single run:

```
test_r_repo_configured  SKIPPED  29.0s
  ↳ Package Manager URL is not configured in vip.toml; cannot verify R repos
```

Two things are wrong with this.

**It burns 29 seconds to decide nothing.** The skip is raised in the `@then` step (`src/vip_tests/workbench/test_packages.py:162`), not in a `@given`. By the time it fires, the test has already signed in, launched a session and run `getOption('repos')` inside R. It does the entire body of work and then declines to assert on the result.

**It is a green gate slot with zero coverage.** #421 existed specifically to stop required checks reporting green while their tests were skipped, and this file has been sitting inside the gated set the whole time doing exactly that.

## Options

1. **Point the config at public Posit Package Manager.** `workbench-smoke.yml` generates `vip.toml`, so it can set `[package_manager] url`. The Workbench images default their `repos.conf` at `packagemanager.posit.co`, so this likely makes the assertion meaningful with no extra container. Needs verifying against the image rather than assumed — check what `getOption('repos')` actually returns in the container before relying on it.
2. **Stand up a Package Manager container alongside Workbench.** Truthful but expensive, and it duplicates what `packagemanager-smoke.yml` already covers. Probably only worth it as part of the cross-product work in #540.
3. **Drop it from the `gate` tier and leave it in `full`.** Cheapest, and honest about what the gate covers, but the test still skips wherever it runs, so it remains dead weight rather than coverage.

Option 1 first, falling back to 3 if the repos URL does not line up.

## Acceptance

- `test_r_repo_configured` either executes and asserts, or is removed from the gated set — not both skipping and gating.
- If the fix is option 1, the passing result is confirmed in the `smoke-results.xml` artifact rather than inferred from a green job.
- Whatever is decided is written down in the workflow, so the next person does not have to re-measure it.

## Worth checking elsewhere

This was found by parsing the JUnit artifact for skip reasons. The same audit across the other gated suites would show whether any other required-check test is permanently skipping — `workbench/test_data_sources.py` is already known to skip on "No data sources configured in vip.toml", and it is also in the gated set.

title: [Feature] Populate [runtimes] in the CI Workbench config so test_runtime_versions runs
description:
Child of #409. Found while measuring the Workbench suite for #539.

`workbench/test_runtime_versions.py` contributes three tests, and all three skip on every run — not because a Docker Workbench cannot support them, but because the generated config omits one section:

```
test_r_versions          SKIPPED — No expected R versions specified in vip.toml [runtimes]
test_r_version_in_session SKIPPED — No expected R versions specified in vip.toml [runtimes]
test_python_versions     SKIPPED — No expected Python versions specified in vip.toml [runtimes]
```

This is free coverage. `workbench-smoke.yml` writes `vip.toml` from scratch, so it can populate `[runtimes]` with whatever the container actually ships.

## Scope

`RuntimesConfig` (`src/vip/config.py:390`) takes `r_versions` and `python_versions` as lists of version strings. The Workbench image installs runtimes under `/opt/R` and `/opt/python`, so the workflow can enumerate them from the running container and write them into the config before pytest starts.

Sketch, to be verified against the real image layout:

```bash
R_VERSIONS=$(docker exec "$CID" ls /opt/R 2>/dev/null | jq -R . | jq -sc .)
PY_VERSIONS=$(docker exec "$CID" ls /opt/python 2>/dev/null | jq -R . | jq -sc .)
```

Then emit a `[runtimes]` block into the generated `vip.toml`.

## Watch out

Populating `[runtimes]` from the same container the tests then assert against makes the check partly tautological — it proves the versions Workbench reports in-session match what is installed on disk, which is a real check (`test_r_version_in_session` runs R and compares), but it cannot catch "the wrong runtimes were installed". That is the correct scope for a container smoke test; pinning expected versions is a customer-deployment concern.

These belong in the `full` tier at minimum. Whether they are fast enough for the PR gate depends on whether each spawns a session — `test_r_version_in_session` does, so budget roughly 30s for it.

## Acceptance

- `workbench-smoke.yml` writes a `[runtimes]` block derived from the running container.
- The three `test_runtime_versions` tests execute rather than skip, verified in the `smoke-results.xml` artifact.
- The tier placement (gate vs full) is chosen from the measured runtime, and recorded in the workflow.

title: [Feature] Terminate TLS in front of a product in CI so the HTTPS/SSL suites can run
description:
Child of #409 (robust CI/CD epic). Split out of #540.

`security/test_https.py` and `cross_product/test_ssl.py` can never run in CI as things stand, because both bail out unless the product URL is HTTPS:

```
src/vip_tests/security/test_https.py:48    if not pc.url.startswith("https://"):
src/vip_tests/cross_product/test_ssl.py:40  if parsed.scheme != "https":
```

The containers the smoke workflows stand up serve plain HTTP, so adding these files as-is would produce a green run made entirely of skips — the same green-with-no-coverage pattern #421 was about. They need TLS terminating in front of a product before they mean anything.

## Between them these cover

- HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect enforcement (`test_https`).
- Certificate validity, including expiry (`test_ssl`).
- That plain HTTP is not silently served alongside HTTPS.

Worth having: TLS misconfiguration is a common real-world install problem, and these are the only tests that check it.

## Scope

- Terminate TLS in front of one containerized product — Connect is the natural choice, since `connect-smoke.yml` is already the richest workflow.
- A reverse-proxy sidecar (Caddy or nginx) with a self-signed cert is the obvious approach; Caddy needs the least configuration for a self-signed local cert.
- The suite must be given the HTTPS URL, and `tls.insecure` must stay unset — `test_ssl.py:45` skips the certificate-validity check when `tls.insecure = true`, so setting it to swallow self-signed warnings would defeat the point. That means the CA needs to be trusted, not bypassed.

## Open questions

- Self-signed with an explicitly trusted CA, or a real cert via a test domain? Self-signed plus trusted CA keeps it hermetic; the trade is that the trust plumbing has to work for both httpx and Playwright.
- Does this justify its own workflow, or a second job inside `connect-smoke.yml`? A separate job keeps the fast PR gate fast.
- Should the expiry assertion in `test_ssl` be given a deliberately short-lived cert so the check is proven to work, rather than trivially passing on a 10-year self-signed cert?

## Acceptance

- `test_https` and `test_ssl` execute against a real TLS endpoint in CI, with certificate validation genuinely on.
- The run shows real passes, not skips — verified by confirming the tests fail when the proxy is misconfigured.

title: selftests: test_small_uses_threadpool fails on local macOS due to mock server listen backlog
description:
## Summary

`selftests/test_load_engine.py::TestAutoRouting::test_small_uses_threadpool` fails reliably when the selftests are run on a local macOS machine. It passes on GitHub's macOS runners, so CI is green and this is not currently blocking merges — but it breaks the `uv run pytest selftests/` workflow documented in `CLAUDE.md` for anyone developing on macOS.

## Symptom

The test asserts `result.failure_rate == 0.0` after issuing 50 concurrent requests at a local mock HTTP server. The observed failure rate varies per run:

```
run0: failure_rate=0.58  errors={'[Errno 54] Connection reset by peer': 28, '[Errno 22] Invalid argument': 1}
run1: failure_rate=0.82  errors={'[Errno 54] Connection reset by peer': 41}
run2: failure_rate=0.48  errors={'[Errno 54] Connection reset by peer': 24}
run3: failure_rate=0.48  errors={'[Errno 54] Connection reset by peer': 24}
run4: failure_rate=0.60  errors={'[Errno 54] Connection reset by peer': 30}
```

The varying number is why this looks like a timing flake, but it is not — `failure_rate` is the fraction of HTTP requests that genuinely failed, and every failure is a connection reset.

## Cause

The `mock_server` fixture's `_ThreadedHTTPServer` inherits `request_queue_size = 5` from `socketserver.TCPServer`. That value is the `listen()` backlog. The test opens 50 connections near-simultaneously, so connections beyond the backlog are reset before they are accepted.

The existing comment above `_skip_high_concurrency_on_macos` already identifies the underlying cause ("tighter ephemeral port range and listen backlog than Linux"), but the mitigation was to skip macOS for the 100+ request async tests rather than to raise the backlog. `test_small_uses_threadpool` issues 50 requests and carries no skip, so it remains exposed.

## Verified fix

Setting an adequate backlog on the fixture's server class eliminates the failures:

```python
class _ThreadedHTTPServer(http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer):
    allow_reuse_address = True
    daemon_threads = True
    request_queue_size = 128
```

Result with that one line changed, same 50-request load, 5 consecutive runs:

```
run0: failure_rate=0.00
run1: failure_rate=0.00
run2: failure_rate=0.00
run3: failure_rate=0.00
run4: failure_rate=0.00
```

## Additional benefit

If the backlog is the real constraint, this may also allow the two `_skip_high_concurrency_on_macos` skips to be removed, restoring macOS coverage of the async load path (currently only exercised on Linux). That should be verified separately at 200 requests rather than assumed, since the ephemeral port range is a distinct limit from the listen backlog and may still bite at higher concurrency.

## Reproduction

On macOS:

```bash
uv run pytest selftests/test_load_engine.py::TestAutoRouting::test_small_uses_threadpool -p no:vip -v
```

`-p no:vip` is needed to see the real assertion values, since VIP's own pytest plugin replaces tracebacks with a one-line concise error.

title: [Bug] vip cleanup and vip uninstall cannot reach a Connect with an untrusted certificate
description:
Neither `vip cleanup` nor `vip uninstall` accepts `--insecure` or `--ca-bundle`, and neither reads `[tls]` settings for its own HTTP calls, so against a deployment using a self-signed or internal-CA certificate they fail with no way to proceed. `vip verify` supports both.

Surfaced while fixing #537: scheme resolution now correctly refuses to downgrade to plaintext when a TLS listener is present but untrusted, and prints guidance naming `[tls] insecure` / `[tls] ca_bundle`. For `cleanup` and `uninstall` that guidance is only half-actionable -- the config keys exist, but these commands have no flag equivalents, and a user passing `--connect-url` with no `vip.toml` has nowhere to set them.

title: [Bug] _create_api_key_via_session crashes with AttributeError when a proxy 301/302-redirects the key-creation POST
description:
## Symptom

`vip verify`'s auth setup crashes instead of degrading gracefully:

```
AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'
  src/vip/auth.py:1576  api_key = create_resp.json().get("key")
```

The function documents "returns the API key string, or None on failure" and catches `(httpx.HTTPError, ValueError, KeyError)`. `AttributeError` is not in that tuple, so it escapes and takes the run down.

## Cause

When a reverse proxy redirects `POST /__api__/v1/users/{guid}/keys` with **301 or 302** (not 307/308), httpx downgrades POST to GET while following it, exactly as browsers and curl do. The downgraded GET lands on the same path, which is Connect's key-*listing* route, and that returns a JSON array. `.get("key")` on a list raises.

A redirect on the earlier `GET /v1/user` does not trigger this -- GET stays GET whatever the redirect code.

## Reproduction

A plaintext HTTP server that redirects every method to an HTTPS Connect endpoint with status 301 (rather than 307), then calling `_create_api_key_via_session(page, http_url, "test_vip_key", insecure=True)`, hits the traceback reliably.

A blanket `return 301` for all methods is a common nginx pattern, so this is reachable in ordinary deployments.

## Relationship to #537

Adding `follow_redirects=True` to the mint client (needed to fix #537) is what makes this reachable. Previously a redirect on the POST simply came back as not-success and the function returned None gracefully. It is a real crash either way, but it did not exist as a live path before that change.

## Suggested fix

An `isinstance(..., dict)` guard on the parsed response before `.get("key")`, matching the guard `_resolve_connect_api_base` already applies, plus `AttributeError` in the caught tuple or an explicit shape check.

title: [Bug] Release commits never relock, so every `uv run` dirties uv.lock in a way the Lockfile Guard rejects
description:
## Symptom

A clean checkout of `main` becomes dirty as soon as you run any `uv` command:

```
$ git status --short
 M uv.lock
$ git diff uv.lock
-version = "0.58.9"
+version = "0.58.10"
```

The change is `uv.lock`'s own `posit-vip` entry. Reverting it and running `uv run` again reproduces it immediately.

## Cause

`chore(release)` commits bump the version in `pyproject.toml` and `src/vip/__init__.py` but never relock. Checked the last five: `c84b2185` (0.58.10), `bb4b2e74`, `f64886e4`, `7663a3a8`, `f7970efd` all touch exactly `CHANGELOG.md`, `pyproject.toml`, `src/vip/__init__.py`. So on `main` today `pyproject.toml` says `0.58.10` while `uv.lock` says `0.58.9`, and `uv` corrects the lock the moment it resolves anything.

## Why it is more than cosmetic

The Lockfile Guard in `ci.yml` rejects a PR that changes `uv.lock` without also changing `pyproject.toml`. That rule is right for its purpose (catching stale lockfiles carried in by bot PRs), but it means nobody can fix this drift directly -- a lockfile-only PR is blocked by design. The correction can only ride along on an unrelated dependency PR, which is how #556 came to carry it.

Day to day it means every contributor works with a permanently dirty file they must remember to `git checkout --` before staging, and any agent or script that stages broadly can silently commit it and trip the guard.

## Candidate fixes

1. Relock as part of the release commit, so the lock never lags. Most direct, and keeps the invariant that a clean checkout is clean.
2. Exempt the `posit-vip` self-version from the guard, since a version-only change to the project's own entry carries no dependency risk.
3. Stop writing the project version into `uv.lock`, if uv offers that.

Option 1 looks right, but it touches the release workflow, so it deserves a deliberate decision rather than a drive-by change.
